```tsx
router.post("/", () => new Response("posted"))

const server = new Server(router)
server.serve("127.0.0.1", 3205)

const base = "http://127.0.0.1:3205"
console.log((await fetch(`${base}/`).then(response => response.text())))
console.log((await fetch(`${base}/admin/dashboard`).then(response => response.text())))
console.log((await fetch(`${base}/admin/dashboard`, {headers: {authorization: "secret"}}).then(response => response.text())))
const posted = await fetch(`${base}/`, {method: "POST"})
console.log(await posted.text(), posted.headers.get("x-inspected"))

server.close()
```
Output:

```text
logged: 200 GET / (took under a second)
public
logged: 401 GET /admin/dashboard (took under a second)
Not allowed
logged: 200 GET /admin/dashboard (took under a second)
the dashboard
logged: 200 POST / (took under a second)
posted post
```
Common uses are logging and timing (a request inspector that records the start in the [metadata](/docs/veloserver/request-metadata/), and a response inspector that logs), authentication (a request inspector that returns a `401`), and setting headers on every response.

---

Source: https://velotype.github.io/docs/veloserver/static-files/

# Static files

`router.mountFiles(mountPath, targetDir, memoized = true)` serves a directory, and `router.mountFile(mountPath, targetFile, memoized = true)` serves a single file. Both serve on GET, and both are async, so `await` them before serving.

By default (`memoized` true) files are read once, when they are mounted, and held in memory. Each is served with an ETag, and with a gzip-compressed copy for clients that accept it. Pass `false` to read the file on each request instead, which suits files that change while the server runs.

```tsx
import { Router, Server } from "@velotype/veloserver"

// Make a directory to serve
const dir = await Deno.makeTempDir()
await Deno.writeTextFile(`${dir}/app.js`, "console.log('hello from app.js')\n".repeat(50))
await Deno.writeTextFile(`${dir}/style.css`, "body { margin: 0 }\n")
await Deno.writeTextFile(`${dir}/favicon.ico`, "icon")

const router = new Router<never>({})

// mountFiles() serves a directory, and mountFile() a single file. Both serve on GET.
// By default files are read once and held in memory, with an ETag and a gzip-compressed copy for
// clients that accept it. Pass false as the last argument to read the file on each request.
await router.mountFiles("/build/", dir + "/", true)
await router.mountFile("/favicon.ico", `${dir}/favicon.ico`, false)

const server = new Server(router)
server.serve("127.0.0.1", 3206)

const base = "http://127.0.0.1:3206"
const js = await fetch(`${base}/build/app.js`)
console.log("app.js:", js.status, js.headers.get("content-type"), js.headers.get("content-encoding") ?? "no encoding")
console.log("has an ETag:", js.headers.has("etag"))
await js.body?.cancel()

const css = await fetch(`${base}/build/style.css`)
console.log("style.css:", css.status, JSON.stringify(await css.text()))

const icon = await fetch(`${base}/favicon.ico`)
console.log("favicon.ico:", icon.status, JSON.stringify(await icon.text()))

server.close()
await Deno.remove(dir, {recursive: true})
```
Output:

```text
app.js: 200 text/javascript; charset=UTF-8 gzip
has an ETag: true
style.css: 200 "body { margin: 0 }\n"
favicon.ico: 200 "icon"
```

---

Source: https://velotype.github.io/docs/veloserver/running-the-server/

# Running the server

## Shutting down

`serve()` registers listeners for `SIGINT`, `SIGTERM`, and `SIGUSR1`, and releases them once the server has finished shutting down. With nothing else pending, the process then ends on its own.

`server.close(reason?)` stops the server from code.

| Member | Description |
|---|---|
| `serve(hostname, port, options?)` | Starts the server. `options.exitProcessOnClose` calls `Deno.exit(0)` the moment the server has finished shutting down, even with other work pending (default: `false`) |
| `close(reason?)` | Stops the server. The reason is logged |
| `addServerListenCallback(callback)` | Runs `callback` just after the server starts listening |
| `addServerFinishedCallback(callback)` | Runs `callback` just after the server has finished |

Leave `exitProcessOnClose` unset when the server is one part of a longer-lived process, such as a test suite or a build step, which should carry on after the server stops.

```tsx
import { Router, Server } from "@velotype/veloserver"

const router = new Router<never>({})
router.get("/", () => new Response("hello"))

const server = new Server(router)

// Run code when the server starts listening, and when it has finished
server.addServerListenCallback(() => console.log("callback: listening"))
server.addServerFinishedCallback(() => console.log("callback: finished"))

// serve() registers listeners for SIGINT, SIGTERM, and SIGUSR1, and releases them once the server
// has finished shutting down. With nothing else pending, the process then ends on its own.
// Pass exitProcessOnClose: true to end the process the moment the server stops, even with other
// work still pending.
server.serve("127.0.0.1", 3207, {exitProcessOnClose: false})

await fetch("http://127.0.0.1:3207/").then(response => response.text())

// close() stops the server from code. The reason is logged.
server.close("done with the example")
```
Output:

```text
callback: listening
callback: finished
```
## Development server

`@velotype/veloserver/dev` exports `DevServer`, which serves a [Velotype](/docs/velotype/) app during development and updates the page when its files change.

```tsx
import { Router, Server } from "@velotype/veloserver"
import { DevServer } from "@velotype/veloserver/dev"

// Serves a Velotype app during development, and updates the page when its files change.
// Run it with --allow-net --allow-read --allow-write --allow-run --allow-env: builds run
// `deno bundle` and write temporary files.
const dev = new DevServer({
    // module: serve each module unbundled, and re-run only the changed ones, keeping component state
    // bundle: rebuild the bundle and re-run it, keeping component state
    // reload: rebuild the bundle and reload the page
    // off:    no development routes. The page loads the production scripts.
    mode: "module",
    // The browser entry module, relative to root
    entry: "./browser/main.tsx",
    // Optional: root (default: the current directory), config, watch, velotype, and production
})

const router = new Router<never>({})
await dev.mount(router)

// pageScripts() writes the scripts for the current mode, so switching modes needs no change to the page
router.get("/", () => new Response(`<!DOCTYPE html><html><body><div id="app"></div>${dev.pageScripts()}</body></html>`,
    {headers: {"content-type": "text/html; charset=utf-8"}}))

const server = new Server(router)
// Watching files keeps the process running, so stop it with the server
server.addServerFinishedCallback(() => dev.close())
server.serve("localhost", 3000)
```
### Modes

`mode` sets how the page is updated when a file changes:

| Mode | Serves | On a change |
|---|---|---|
| `module` | each module unbundled, transpiled on request | re-runs the changed modules, and the components on the page keep their state |
| `bundle` | the app bundle | rebuilds and re-runs the bundle, and the components on the page keep their state |
| `reload` | the app bundle | rebuilds the bundle and reloads the page |
| `off` | the `production` scripts | nothing, and no development routes are added |

`pageScripts()` writes the scripts for the current mode, so switching modes needs no change to the page. In `off` mode it writes the `production` option's import map and scripts:

```tsx
import { Router } from "@velotype/veloserver"
import { DevServer } from "@velotype/veloserver/dev"

// In mode "off" there are no development routes, and pageScripts() writes the production option's
// import map and scripts. The same page code serves development and production.
const dev = new DevServer({
    mode: "off",
    entry: "./browser/main.tsx",
    production: {
        importMap: {"@velotype/velotype": "/build/velotype.js"},
        scripts: ["/build/velotype.js", "/build/main.js"],
    },
})
await dev.mount(new Router<never>({}))

console.log(dev.mode)
console.log(dev.pageScripts())
dev.close()
```
Output:

```text
off
<script type="importmap">{"imports":{"@velotype/velotype":"/build/velotype.js"}}</script>
<script type="module" src="/build/velotype.js"></script>
<script type="module" src="/build/main.js"></script>
```
### Options

| Option | Description |
|---|---|
| `mode` | The `DevMode`. Required |
| `entry` | The browser entry module, relative to `root`. Required |
| `root` | The project directory, which contains `deno.json` (default: the current directory) |
| `config` | The project's config file, relative to `root` (default: `deno.json` or `deno.jsonc`) |
| `watch` | Directories to watch, relative to `root` (default: the entry module's directory) |
| `velotype` | The Velotype package specifier that the dev runtime is loaded from (default: `compilerOptions.jsxImportSource` from `deno.json`, or `@velotype/velotype`) |
| `production` | `{importMap?, scripts}`: the page scripts for mode `off` |

### How hot updates work

Hot updates use the Velotype dev runtime (`@velotype/velotype/jsx-dev-runtime`), so builds use `"jsx": "react-jsxdev"` whatever `deno.json` sets. The project's own setting can stay `react-jsx` for production builds. Every Velotype import loads one shared copy of the dev runtime, served at `/__velo/velotype.js`.

In `module` mode a changed module is updated on its own when all of its exports are components, or when it calls `import.meta.hot.accept()`. Otherwise the modules that import it run again, and the page reloads when the change reaches the entry module. `import.meta.hot.dispose(callback)` runs `callback(import.meta.hot.data)` before a module runs again, to release what it set up.

A build error is logged in the browser, and the page keeps running the last working code. When the server restarts, the page reloads.

What Velotype does with a hot update is in [Development tools](/docs/velotype/development-tools/#hot-reloading). The [hot-reload-demo](https://github.com/Velotype/example-velotype-projects/tree/main/hot-reload-demo) is an app that runs in each mode.

---

Source: https://velotype.github.io/docs/veloserver/api-reference/

# API reference

Everything `@velotype/veloserver` and `@velotype/veloserver/dev` export.

## Router

`class Router<ContextMetadata>`

`new Router({not_found_handler?, bad_request_error_handler?, server_error_handler?, context_metadata_constructor?})`

| Member | Description |
|---|---|
| `get(paths, handler)` | Adds a handler for HTTP GET on a path or Array of paths |
| `head(paths, handler)` | Adds a handler for HTTP HEAD |
| `post(paths, handler)` | Adds a handler for HTTP POST |
| `addGetInspector(paths, inspector)` | Adds an inspector for GET |
| `addHeadInspector(paths, inspector)` | Adds an inspector for HEAD |
| `addPostInspector(paths, inspector)` | Adds an inspector for POST |
| `addAllInspector(paths, inspector)` | Adds an inspector for GET, HEAD, and POST |
| `mountFile(mountPath, targetFile, memoized = true)` | Serves one file on GET |
| `mountFiles(mountDir, targetDir, memoized = true)` | Serves a directory on GET |
| `json(request, context, data)` | A 200 JSON response |
| `badRequest(request, context)` | The router's 400 response |
| `serverError(request, context)` | The router's 500 response |
| `requestHandler: (request: Request) => Promise<Response>` | Processes a request. It is what `Deno.serve()` is given, and it is bound to the router |

See [Routes](/docs/veloserver/routes/).

## Server

`class Server<ContextMetadata = never>`

| Member | Description |
|---|---|
| `constructor(router)` | Serves all routes in `router` |
| `serve(hostname, port, options?)` | Calls `Deno.serve()`. `ServeOptions` has `exitProcessOnClose?: boolean` |
| `close(reason?)` | Stops the server |
| `addServerListenCallback(callback)` | Runs after the server starts listening |
| `addServerFinishedCallback(callback)` | Runs after the server has finished |

See [Running the server](/docs/veloserver/running-the-server/).

## Context

`class Context<ContextMetadata = undefined>`: `meta`, `pathVariables?`, `url`, `getPathParts()`, and `addPathVariable(name, value)`. See [Request metadata](/docs/veloserver/request-metadata/#context).

## Inspectors

| Export | Description |
|---|---|
| `Inspector<ContextMetadata>` | `new Inspector(requestInspector?, responseInspector?, observeChildPaths = true)` |
| `RequestInspectorResponse` | `new RequestInspectorResponse(response?)`. With a `response`, the request ends early |

See [Inspectors](/docs/veloserver/inspectors/).

## Types

| Type | Definition |
|---|---|
| `Handler<ContextMetadata>` | `(request: Request, context: Context<ContextMetadata>) => Response \| Promise<Response>` |
| `RequestInspector<ContextMetadata>` | `(request: Request, context: Context<ContextMetadata>) => RequestInspectorResponse \| Promise<RequestInspectorResponse>` |
| `ResponseInspector<ContextMetadata>` | `(request: Request, response: Response, context: Context<ContextMetadata>) => void \| Promise<void>` |
| `Callback` | `(() => void) \| (() => Promise<void>)` |
| `ServeOptions` | `{exitProcessOnClose?: boolean}` |

## DevServer

From `@velotype/veloserver/dev`.

`class DevServer`: `new DevServer(options: DevServerOptions)`

| Member | Description |
|---|---|
| `mode: DevMode` | How the page is updated when a file changes |
| `mount(router): Promise<void>` | Adds the development routes to `router`, builds the app, and starts watching its files |
| `pageScripts(): string` | The scripts to write into the app's pages, for the current mode |
| `close(): void` | Stops watching files and closes the connections to browsers |

`type DevMode = "module" | "bundle" | "reload" | "off"`. `DevServerOptions` is in [Running the server](/docs/veloserver/running-the-server/#options).

---

Source: https://velotype.github.io/docs/velossr/

# Getting started

velossr renders TSX to HTML on the server. There is no virtual DOM diffing and no client runtime: components run once per request and produce bytes, either all at once or streamed as async pieces resolve.

It is the server-side version of [Velotype](/docs/velotype/)'s TSX. Use it to send a page's HTML from the server, and use Velotype for the parts of the page that are interactive. Every example in these docs is a file that is type-checked against the published package and run, and the output shown is what the example printed.

## Install

velossr is a [JSR package](https://jsr.io/@velotype/velossr) for Deno. Add it, and point the TSX compiler at it in `deno.json`:

```sh
deno add jsr:@velotype/velossr
```

```json
{
    "compilerOptions": {
        "jsx": "react-jsx",
        "jsxImportSource": "@velotype/velossr"
    }
}
```

A project that has both a server and a browser app needs two JSX settings, because the browser's TSX is Velotype's (`"jsxImportSource": "@velotype/velotype"`). Keep them in separate directories with their own `deno.json`, or set it per file with a `/** @jsxImportSource @velotype/velossr */` comment.

## A page and a server

velossr pairs naturally with [veloserver](/docs/veloserver/). A page is a component, `prepareHTMLVNodeForRendering()` prepares it once, and `renderServerVNode()` renders it for each request.

```tsx
import { type Context, Router, Server } from "@velotype/veloserver"
import { type EmptyAttrs, prepareHTMLVNodeForRendering, renderServerVNode, type StaticServerComponent } from "@velotype/velossr"

const Page: StaticServerComponent<EmptyAttrs> = function() {
    return <html><body><div>Hello velossr!</div></body></html>
}
const preparedPage = prepareHTMLVNodeForRendering(<Page/>)

const router = new Router<never>({})
router.get("/", function(request: Request, context: Context<never>) {
    const response = new Response(renderServerVNode(preparedPage, request, context).toReadableStream())
    response.headers.set("content-type", "text/html; charset=utf-8")
    return response
})

const server = new Server(router)
server.serve("127.0.0.1", 3101)

// Fetch the page once, then stop the server
const response = await fetch("http://127.0.0.1:3101/")
console.log(response.status, response.headers.get("content-type"))
console.log(await response.text())
server.close()
```
Output:

```text
200 text/html; charset=utf-8
<!DOCTYPE html><html><body><div>Hello velossr!</div></body></html>
```
## Writing TSX for the server

Each tag creates a server-side element. Nothing touches a DOM: the element is a description that velossr writes out as HTML.

### Attributes are HTML attributes

velossr writes attributes as strings, so you write TSX the same as if you were writing HTML. Style objects resolve camelCase keys to kebab-case CSS. A `true` boolean attribute is written bare, and a `false` one is left out. Event listener attributes (`onClick`) cannot work on the server: they are left out and a warning is logged.

### Conditional rendering

`false`, `null`, and `undefined` children render nothing, so `{condition && <li/>}` works as it does in Velotype. `true` is written as text. Before velossr 0.0.10 a `false` child was written as the text `false`, so use `{condition ? <li/> : null}` if you are on an older version.

### Fragments

`<>...</>` groups children without a wrapper element.

```tsx
import { renderServerVNode, prepareVNodeForRendering, type ServerVNode } from "@velotype/velossr"

async function show(node: ServerVNode) {
    const bytes = await renderServerVNode(prepareVNodeForRendering(node), new Request("http://localhost/"), {}).toUint8Array()
    console.log(new TextDecoder().decode(bytes))
}

// Attributes are written as HTML attributes
await show(<div class="exampleClass" id="main">this is a div</div>)

// Style objects resolve camelCase keys to kebab-case CSS
await show(<div style={{display: "inline", marginTop: "4px"}}>styled</div>)

// Boolean attributes are written when true, and left out when false
await show(<input type="checkbox" checked={true} disabled={false}/>)

// Text, attribute values, and attribute names are escaped where they are written
const untrusted = `<script>alert("hi")</script> & "quotes"`
await show(<p title={untrusted}>{untrusted}</p>)

// Fragments group children without a wrapper element. false, null, and undefined render nothing,
// so {condition && <li/>} works as it does in Velotype. true is written as text.
const signedIn = false
await show(<ul>{signedIn && <li>Account</li>}<><li>one</li><li>two</li></></ul>)
```
Output:

```text
<div class="exampleClass" id="main">this is a div</div>
<div style="display:inline;margin-top:4px">styled</div>
<input type="checkbox" checked>
<p title="<script>alert(&quot;hi&quot;)</script> &amp; &quot;quotes&quot;">&lt;script>alert(&quot;hi&quot;)&lt;/script> &amp; &quot;quotes&quot;</p>
<ul><li>one</li><li>two</li></ul>
```
## Next steps

* [Components](/docs/velossr/components/): static and dynamic components
* [Rendering](/docs/velossr/rendering/): preparing pages, and sending them whole or streamed
* [Escaping and embedding](/docs/velossr/escaping-and-embedding/): what is escaped, and inline scripts, styles, and JSON
* [Islands](/docs/velossr/islands/): interactive parts of a server-rendered page

---

Source: https://velotype.github.io/docs/velossr/components/

# Components

velossr has two kinds of components. A static component renders the same way every time, and a dynamic component can see the request and wait for data.

## Static components

A `StaticServerComponent<AttrsType>` is a plain function that renders synchronously, with no access to the request. Use it for markup that never depends on the request. It receives its attrs, and its children as a second argument. To accept children, add `ChildrenAttr` to the attrs type.

```tsx
import { type ChildrenAttr, prepareVNodeForRendering, renderServerVNode, type StaticServerComponent } from "@velotype/velossr"

// A StaticServerComponent is a plain function that renders synchronously, with no access to the
// request. Use it for markup that never depends on the request.
const Greeting: StaticServerComponent<{name: string}> = function(attrs) {
    return <div>Hello {attrs.name}!</div>
}

// A Component that accepts children adds ChildrenAttr to its attrs, and takes them as a second argument
const Card: StaticServerComponent<{title: string} & ChildrenAttr> = function(attrs, children) {
    return <section>
        <h2>{attrs.title}</h2>
        {children}
    </section>
}

const page = <Card title="Greetings">
    <Greeting name="Ada"/>
    <Greeting name="Grace"/>
</Card>

const html = await renderServerVNode(prepareVNodeForRendering(page), new Request("http://localhost/"), {}).toUint8Array()
console.log(new TextDecoder().decode(html))
```
Output:

```text
<section><h2>Greetings</h2><div>Hello Ada!</div><div>Hello Grace!</div></section>
```
Static parts of a page are prepared once, when you call [`prepareVNodeForRendering()`](/docs/velossr/rendering/), and then rendered from bytes on every request.

## Dynamic components

A `DynamicServerComponent<AttrsType>` is a class with access to the `Request` and the `context`. Its `render(attrs, children, request, context)` can return a node, or a Promise of one.

If `render()` fails, `onFail(reason, attrs, children, request, context)` renders instead, so one failing component does not take down the rest of the page. By default a failed component renders nothing. Override `onFail()` to show a message.

```tsx
import { DynamicServerComponent, type EmptyAttrs, prepareVNodeForRendering, renderServerVNode, type ServerVNode } from "@velotype/velossr"

type Context = {users: Record<string, string>}

// A DynamicServerComponent is a class with access to the Request and the context. It can render
// synchronously or return a Promise.
class UserGreeting extends DynamicServerComponent<EmptyAttrs> {
    override async render(_attrs: Readonly<EmptyAttrs>, _children: Readonly<ServerVNode[]>, request: Request, context: Context) {
        const id = new URL(request.url).searchParams.get("user") ?? ""
        const name = await Promise.resolve(context.users[id])
        if (!name) {
            throw new Error(`No user ${id}`)
        }
        return <div>Hello {name}!</div>
    }

    // If render() fails, onFail() renders instead, so one failing component does not take down the
    // rest of the page. By default a failed component renders nothing.
    override onFail(reason: Readonly<unknown>) {
        return <div>Hello! ({String(reason)})</div>
    }
}

async function render(url: string) {
    const page = <main><UserGreeting/></main>
    const output = renderServerVNode(prepareVNodeForRendering(page), new Request(url), {users: {1: "Ada"}})
    console.log(new TextDecoder().decode(await output.toUint8Array()))
}

await render("http://localhost/?user=1")
await render("http://localhost/?user=2")
```
Output:

```text
<main><div>Hello Ada!</div></main>
<main><div>Hello! (Error: No user 2)</div></main>
```
The `context` is whatever you pass to `renderServerVNode()`. With veloserver it is the request's `Context`.

## AsyncRenderObject

An `AsyncRenderObject<DataType>` waits on one Promise and can be rendered into several places. It is created with the Promise, the request, and the context: `new AsyncRenderObject(promise, request, context, defaultOnFail?)`.

`render(renderFunction, onFail?)` places it in the page. `renderFunction` receives the resolved value and returns a node, or a Promise of one. `onFail` renders when the Promise rejects or the render function throws. When a place passes no `onFail`, `defaultOnFail` is used, and without either the place renders nothing.

```tsx
import { AsyncRenderObject, DynamicServerComponent, prepareVNodeForRendering, renderServerVNode, type ServerVNode } from "@velotype/velossr"

type User = {name: string, team: string}

class Profile extends DynamicServerComponent<{user: AsyncRenderObject<User>}> {
    override render(attrs: Readonly<{user: AsyncRenderObject<User>}>) {
        // One AsyncRenderObject can be rendered in several places. It waits on one Promise.
        return <div>
            {attrs.user.render(async user => <h1>{user.name}</h1>)}
            {attrs.user.render(async user => <p>Team: {user.team}</p>)}
            {attrs.user.render(
                async () => { throw new Error("not reached") },
                // onFail() renders when the Promise rejects or the render function throws
                (reason: Readonly<unknown>): ServerVNode => <p>Failed: {String(reason)}</p>,
            )}
        </div>
    }
}

const request = new Request("http://localhost/")
const context = {}
const user = new AsyncRenderObject<User>(Promise.resolve({name: "Ada", team: "Analytical"}), request, context)

const page = <Profile user={user}/>
const output = renderServerVNode(prepareVNodeForRendering(page), request, context)
console.log(new TextDecoder().decode(await output.toUint8Array()))
```
Output:

```text
<div><h1>Ada</h1><p>Team: Analytical</p><p>Failed: Error: not reached</p></div>
```
The output of an AsyncRenderObject is escaped as HTML, so it cannot be placed inside a `<script>` or `<style>`. See [Escaping and embedding](/docs/velossr/escaping-and-embedding/).

---

Source: https://velotype.github.io/docs/velossr/rendering/

# Rendering

Rendering a page has two steps: prepare it, which can happen once, and render it for each request.

## Preparing a page

`prepareVNodeForRendering(node)` compacts a node into a flat array of bytes and the parts that need a request. `prepareHTMLVNodeForRendering(node)` does the same with `<!DOCTYPE html>` added at the start, to make a valid HTML document.

Prepare at module load, outside the request handler, so the static parts are not rebuilt for every request.

## Rendering for a request

`renderServerVNode(node, request, context)` takes a prepared page, or a raw node, and returns a `RenderedVDOM`. Convert that into the form you need:

| Method | Returns | For |
|---|---|---|
| `toArrayBuffer()` | `Promise<ArrayBuffer>` | A `Response` that is sent all at once |
| `toUint8Array()` | `Promise<Uint8Array>` | The bytes, for tests or further processing |
| `toReadableStream()` | `ReadableStream` | A `Response` that streams |

```tsx
import { type EmptyAttrs, prepareHTMLVNodeForRendering, renderServerVNode, type StaticServerComponent } from "@velotype/velossr"

const Page: StaticServerComponent<EmptyAttrs> = function() {
    return <html><body><div>Hello velossr!</div></body></html>
}

// Prepare a page once, which can happen at module load outside the request handler. The static
// parts are compacted into bytes. prepareHTMLVNodeForRendering() adds <!DOCTYPE html>, and
// prepareVNodeForRendering() renders a fragment as it is.
const preparedPage = prepareHTMLVNodeForRendering(<Page/>)

const request = new Request("http://localhost/")
const context = {}

// All at once
const all = await renderServerVNode(preparedPage, request, context).toArrayBuffer()
console.log(new TextDecoder().decode(all))

// As a single Uint8Array
const bytes = await renderServerVNode(preparedPage, request, context).toUint8Array()
console.log(bytes.length, "bytes")

// Streamed, where async components flush in place as they resolve
const stream = renderServerVNode(preparedPage, request, context).toReadableStream()
const response = new Response(stream, {headers: {"content-type": "text/html; charset=utf-8"}})
console.log(await response.text())
```
Output:

```text
<!DOCTYPE html><html><body><div>Hello velossr!</div></body></html>
66 bytes
<!DOCTYPE html><html><body><div>Hello velossr!</div></body></html>
```
## Streaming

With `toReadableStream()`, the page is written as it is ready. Static parts go out at once, and an async `DynamicServerComponent` flushes in place when it resolves, so the visitor sees the top of the page before the slow part is done.

```tsx
import { DynamicServerComponent, type EmptyAttrs, prepareHTMLVNodeForRendering, renderServerVNode } from "@velotype/velossr"

// An async component that takes a while
class SlowPart extends DynamicServerComponent<EmptyAttrs> {
    override async render() {
        await new Promise(resolve => setTimeout(resolve, 50))
        return <p>The slow part</p>
    }
}

const page = <html><body>
    <h1>Shown first</h1>
    <SlowPart/>
    <footer>Shown last</footer>
</body></html>

const request = new Request("http://localhost/")
const stream = renderServerVNode(prepareHTMLVNodeForRendering(page), request, {}).toReadableStream()

// Each chunk is written as soon as it is ready, so the page starts arriving before the slow part resolves
const decoder = new TextDecoder()
const start = performance.now()
let html = ""
let firstPartAt = 0
let slowPartAt = 0
for await (const chunk of stream) {
    const text = decoder.decode(chunk)
    html += text
    if (text == "Shown first") {
        firstPartAt = performance.now() - start
    }
    if (text == "The slow part") {
        slowPartAt = performance.now() - start
    }
}

console.log(html)
console.log("The first part arrived before the slow part resolved:", firstPartAt < 40)
console.log("The slow part arrived after it resolved:", slowPartAt >= 40)
```
Output:

```text
<!DOCTYPE html><html><body><h1>Shown first</h1><p>The slow part</p><footer>Shown last</footer></body></html>
The first part arrived before the slow part resolved: true
The slow part arrived after it resolved: true
```
Because the response is already streaming when an async component fails, there is no way to change the status code afterwards. Handle failures with `onFail()`.

---

Source: https://velotype.github.io/docs/velossr/escaping-and-embedding/

# Escaping and embedding

velossr escapes what it writes, so data from a request cannot inject markup.

## What is escaped

Text, attribute values, and attribute names are escaped automatically, including the text that components return (as a string, an Array, or a fragment). Text is escaped once, where it is written.

* In HTML text, `"`, `&`, and `<` are escaped
* In attribute values, quotes and `&` are escaped, including in style object values
* Characters that are not valid in an attribute name are removed

## Inline style and script

Write CSS and JS as plain template strings. Browsers do not decode character references (such as `&lt;`) inside `<style>` and `<script>`, so their text is written as is, with `<`, `>`, and `&` unchanged. Only the sequences that would end the element early are changed, in a way that reads the same in JavaScript and CSS strings:

* in a `<script>`, the `<` of `</script` and `<!--` is written as `<`
* in a `<style>`, `</style` is written as `<\/style`

This also makes JSON safe to embed, whatever its strings contain: `<script type="application/json">{JSON.stringify(data)}</script>`.

A `DynamicServerComponent` inside a `<script>` or `<style>` has its text escaped the same way, so it can write per-request data. Elements, and the output of an `AsyncRenderObject` (which is escaped as HTML), cannot be placed inside a `<script>` or `<style>`: they are skipped, and an error is logged.

## SafeText

For the rare case where you need to emit raw, already-safe content that should not be escaped at all, wrap it in `SafeText`. Use it only when the input text is known to be safe: HTML, CSS, SVG, and JavaScript escaping depends on where the text is written.

```tsx
import { prepareVNodeForRendering, renderServerVNode, SafeText } from "@velotype/velossr"

const data = {note: "</script><script>alert(1)</script>", amount: 5}

const page = <html>
    <head>
        {/* CSS and JS are plain template strings. They are written as is, and only the
            sequences that would end the element early are changed. */}
        <style>{`
div > p { color: red; }
/* </style> in text is made safe */
`}</style>
    </head>
    <body>
        <script>{`
function greet(name) {
    if (name.length > 0 && name !== "</script>") {
        console.log("Hello " + name);
    }
}
`}</script>
        {/* This makes JSON safe to embed, whatever its strings contain */}
        <script type="application/json" id="page-data">{JSON.stringify(data)}</script>
        {/* SafeText is not escaped at all: use it only for content that is known to be safe */}
        <div>{new SafeText("<b>already safe</b>")}</div>
    </body>
</html>

const html = await renderServerVNode(prepareVNodeForRendering(page), new Request("http://localhost/"), {}).toUint8Array()
console.log(new TextDecoder().decode(html))
```
Output:

```text
<html><head><style>
div > p { color: red; }
/* <\/style> in text is made safe */
</style></head><body><script>
function greet(name) {
    if (name.length > 0 && name !== "\u003c/script>") {
        console.log("Hello " + name);
    }
}
</script><script type="application/json" id="page-data">{"note":"\u003c/script><script>alert(1)\u003c/script>","amount":5}</script><div><b>already safe</b></div></body></html>
```

---

Source: https://velotype.github.io/docs/velossr/islands/

# Islands

A page can be mostly static HTML from the server, with interactive parts, called islands, that Velotype takes over in the browser.

There is no hydration step that turns the server's HTML into live components. The server renders the markup for each island, and the data its component is created with. The browser then creates the component from the data and swaps it in with `replaceElementWithRoot()`. The server's HTML is shown until the swap, which happens in one step when the page's script runs.

## The server half

The server writes two things for each island: its markup, in an element with an `id`, and its data, as JSON in a `<script type="application/json">` next to it. The JSON is written so that no string in it can end the script early, which is why the data below can contain `</script>`.

Keep the server's markup the same structure as what the browser component renders, so that nothing moves when the island is replaced.

```tsx
import { type ChildrenAttr, prepareHTMLVNodeForRendering, renderServerVNode, type ServerVNode, type StaticServerComponent } from "@velotype/velossr"

type CounterData = {start: number, label: string}

// The server's markup for the counter, the same structure the client Component renders
const CounterMarkup: StaticServerComponent<CounterData> = function(attrs) {
    return <div class="counter"><span>{attrs.label}: {attrs.start}</span><input name="note"/><button type="button">+1</button></div>
}

/** Server-rendered markup for a client Component, and the data the client creates it with */
const Island: StaticServerComponent<{id: string, data: unknown} & ChildrenAttr> = function(attrs, children): ServerVNode {
    return [
        <div id={attrs.id}>{children}</div>,
        <script type="application/json" id={attrs.id + "-data"}>{JSON.stringify(attrs.data)}</script>,
    ]
}

const data: CounterData = {start: 5, label: "Clicks </script> & <b>"}
const page = <html><body>
    <Island id="counter" data={data}><CounterMarkup {...data}/></Island>
    <script type="module" src="/main.js"></script>
</body></html>

const output = renderServerVNode(prepareHTMLVNodeForRendering(page), new Request("http://localhost/"), {})
console.log(new TextDecoder().decode(await output.toUint8Array()))
```
Output:

```text
<!DOCTYPE html><html><body><div id="counter"><div class="counter"><span>Clicks &lt;/script> &amp; &lt;b>: 5</span><input name="note"><button type="button">+1</button></div></div><script type="application/json" id="counter-data">{"start":5,"label":"Clicks \u003c/script> & <b>"}</script><script type="module" src="/main.js"></script></body></html>
```
## The browser half

The browser half is in the [Velotype docs](/docs/velotype/server-rendering/). It reads each island's data, creates the component, copies what the visitor typed into the server's form fields, and swaps the element in.

---

Source: https://velotype.github.io/docs/velossr/api-reference/

# API reference

Everything `@velotype/velossr` exports, by area.

## Rendering

| Export | Signature |
|---|---|
| [`prepareVNodeForRendering`](/docs/velossr/rendering/#preparing-a-page) | `(node: ServerVNode) => PreparedServerVNode` |
| [`prepareHTMLVNodeForRendering`](/docs/velossr/rendering/#preparing-a-page) | `(node: ServerVNode) => PreparedServerVNode`, with `<!DOCTYPE html>` added |
| [`renderServerVNode`](/docs/velossr/rendering/#rendering-for-a-request) | `(node: ServerVNode \| PreparedServerVNode, request: Request, context: any) => RenderedVDOM` |

### RenderedVDOM

| Member | Description |
|---|---|
| `toArrayBuffer(): Promise<ArrayBuffer>` | The whole page, for a `Response` sent all at once |
| `toUint8Array(): Promise<Uint8Array>` | The whole page as bytes |
| `toReadableStream(): ReadableStream` | The page as a stream, for a `Response` that streams |
| `node: RenderedVNode` | The rendered node this wraps |

## Components

### StaticServerComponent

`type StaticServerComponent<AttrsType> = (attrs: Readonly<AttrsType>, children: ServerVNode[]) => ServerVNode | null | undefined`

### DynamicServerComponent

`abstract class DynamicServerComponent<AttrsType>`

| Member | Description |
|---|---|
| `attrs: Readonly<AttrsType>` | The attrs the component was created with |
| `children: Readonly<ServerVNode[]>` | The children the component was created with |
| `abstract render(attrs, children, request, context): ServerVNode \| Promise<ServerVNode>` | Renders the component |
| `onFail(reason, attrs, children, request, context): ServerVNode` | Renders when an async `render()` fails. Renders nothing by default |

See [Components](/docs/velossr/components/#dynamic-components).

### AsyncRenderObject

`class AsyncRenderObject<DataType>`

| Member | Description |
|---|---|
| `constructor(promise, request, context, defaultOnFail?)` | Waits on `promise` |
| `render(renderFunction, onFail?): AsyncRenderedVNodeElement` | Places the resolved value in the page |
| `promise`, `request`, `context`, `defaultOnFail` | What it was created with |

## Text

| Export | Description |
|---|---|
| `SafeText` | `new SafeText(text)`: text that is written without escaping. Use only for content that is known to be safe |
| `ComponentText` | Text from a component's output that is not escaped yet. Created by velossr, and escaped once where it is written |

## Nodes

| Export | Description |
|---|---|
| `ServerVNode` | A node a component can return: an element, text, a number, `null`, `undefined`, or an Array of them |
| `PreparedServerVNode` | A node after preparing: bytes and the parts that need a request |
| `HTMLElement` | The server-side representation of an element, `new HTMLElement(tag, attrs, children)` |
| `DynamicVNodeElement`, `AsyncRenderedVNodeElement`, `RenderedVNode` | Internal nodes for dynamic and async parts |
| `createElement`, `createFragment` | What TSX compiles tags and fragments to |
| `jsx`, `jsxs`, `Fragment` | The automatic JSX runtime |

## Types

| Type | Description |
|---|---|
| `EmptyAttrs` | The attrs type of a component with no attrs |
| `ChildrenAttr` | Add it to a component's attrs type to accept children |
| `BasicTypes` | `string \| bigint \| number \| boolean` |

The package also exports the DOM and JSX types that type-check TSX.

## Entry points

| Import | For |
|---|---|
| `@velotype/velossr` | The runtime |
| `@velotype/velossr/jsx-runtime` | The production JSX runtime |
| `@velotype/velossr/jsx-dev-runtime` | The development JSX runtime |

---

Source: https://velotype.github.io/docs/velotype/

# Getting started

Velotype is a TSX framework that creates real DOM elements as your code runs. There is no virtual DOM and no reconciler, so the elements you create are the ones on the page, and a value that changes renders only the part of the page that depends on it.

This guide installs Velotype, mounts an app, and covers the basics of writing TSX with it. Every example in these docs is a file that is type-checked against the published package, and run in a browser, so what you see compiles and runs.

## Install

Velotype is a [JSR package](https://jsr.io/@velotype/velotype) for Deno, and its code is bundled for the browser. Add it to a Deno project, and point the TSX compiler at it in `deno.json`:

```sh
deno add jsr:@velotype/velotype
```

```json
{
    "compilerOptions": {
        "jsx": "react-jsx",
        "jsxImportSource": "@velotype/velotype",
        "lib": ["dom", "deno.ns", "esnext"]
    }
}
```

`"jsx": "react-jsxdev"` uses the development runtime instead, which supports [hot reloading](/docs/velotype/development-tools/#hot-reloading).

Velotype is about 21kb minified and 7.7kb gzipped for the whole runtime, and bundlers drop the parts an app does not import. Bundle it with `deno bundle` or any bundler that supports Deno specifiers.

## Mounting an app

`replaceElementWithRoot(root, element)` replaces an element that is already in the page with the app's root element and mounts its Components. It accepts `null`, so the result of `document.getElementById()` can be passed directly. It returns the new root element.

`removeElementRoot(element)` is its counterpart: it unmounts and releases the Components and RenderObjects in `element`, then removes it. Velotype only unmounts what it removes itself, so content that is removed with DOM methods is not unmounted.

```tsx
import { Component, type EmptyAttrs, removeElementRoot, replaceElementWithRoot } from "@velotype/velotype"

class App extends Component<EmptyAttrs> {
    override render() {
        return <h1>Hello Velotype</h1>
    }
}

// Replace the placeholder element with the app. The Components in it are mounted.
// replaceElementWithRoot() accepts null, so getElementById() can be passed directly.
const root = replaceElementWithRoot(<App/>, document.getElementById("app"))

// A Dialog, widget, or any part of a page that other code manages can hold Velotype content too:
// insert a placeholder there, then replace it.
const placeholder = document.createElement("div")
document.body.append(placeholder)
const dialogContent = replaceElementWithRoot(<App/>, placeholder)

// removeElementRoot() unmounts and releases the Components in an element, then removes it.
// Use it before other code removes content that Velotype put on the page.
removeElementRoot(dialogContent)
removeElementRoot(root)
```
`replaceElementWithRoot()` is not limited to the app's root element. To add Velotype content to a part of the page that other code manages (such as a dialog or a third-party widget), insert a placeholder element there and replace it. Call `removeElementRoot()` before that code removes the content.

## Writing TSX

TSX is a way to write element creation that looks like HTML. In Velotype each tag creates an element, so its value is an `HTMLElement` and you can use it like any other.

```tsx
// TSX creates real DOM elements, so every one of these is an HTMLElement.
const heading: HTMLHeadingElement = <h1 class="title">Attributes are HTML attributes</h1>

// Style objects are type checked: property names, keywords, units, and colors.
// lowerCamelCase and hyphen-case both work, and so do custom properties.
const styled: HTMLDivElement = <div style={{
    display: "inline-block",
    marginTop: "4px",
    "margin-bottom": "4px",
    "--brand-color": "#336699",
    color: "var(--brand-color)",
    opacity: 0.8,
    width: "calc(100% - 2rem)",
    zIndex: 2,
}}>An object of styles</div>

// Attributes that start with "on" add event listeners
const clicked: HTMLButtonElement = <button type="button" onClick={() => console.log("clicked")}>Click me</button>

// Pass {handler, options} to set addEventListener() options
const once: HTMLButtonElement = <button type="button" onClick={{handler: () => console.log("clicked once"), options: {once: true}}}>Click me once</button>

// on- listens for a custom event by its exact name
const custom: HTMLDivElement = <div on-my-event={() => console.log("my-event received")}></div>
custom.dispatchEvent(new CustomEvent("my-event"))

// false, null, and undefined render nothing
const showDetails = false
const conditional: HTMLDivElement = <div>{showDetails && <div>Details</div>}</div>

// Fragments group children without a wrapper element, and return them as an Array
const items = <><li>one</li><li>two</li></>
const list: HTMLUListElement = <ul>{items}</ul>

// Arrays of elements are children too
const names = ["Ada", "Grace", "Katherine"]
const people: HTMLUListElement = <ul>{names.map(name => <li>{name}</li>)}</ul>

document.body.append(heading, styled, clicked, once, custom, conditional, list, people)
```
### Elements are real elements

A tag such as `<div>` evaluates to an `HTMLDivElement`. You can read its properties, call its methods, and append it with DOM APIs.

### Attributes are HTML attributes

Velotype sets attributes the way HTML does, so you write `class` rather than `className`, and `for` rather than `htmlFor`.

### Style objects

The `style` attribute takes an object. Property names must be CSS properties, in lowerCamelCase (`marginTop`) or hyphen-case (`"margin-top"`), or custom properties (`"--brand-color"`). The values of commonly used properties are checked too: keywords must be ones the property accepts, lengths and times need a unit, and colors must be a named color, `#hex`, or a color function. Numbers are accepted only for properties that take no unit, such as `opacity` and `zIndex`. A value can end with ` !important`, and values using `var()`, `calc()` and other CSS functions are always accepted.

### Event listeners

Attributes that start with `on` add event listeners with `addEventListener()`: `onClick` listens for `click`. Pass `{handler, options}` to set the `addEventListener()` options. Use `on-` followed by the exact name to listen for a custom event, such as `on-my-event`.

### Conditional rendering

`false`, `null`, and `undefined` children render nothing, so `{condition && <div/>}` works as expected.

### Fragments

`<>...</>` groups children without a wrapper element. It returns them as an Array that can be used as children.

## Next steps

* [Components](/docs/velotype/components/): function components, class components, and their lifecycle
* [RenderObjects](/docs/velotype/render-objects/): values that update the page in place
* [Lists](/docs/velotype/lists/): lists that render, move, and remove only the rows that changed

---

Source: https://velotype.github.io/docs/velotype/components/

# Components

Components are the objects that you create as tags in TSX. Velotype has two kinds: function components for simple, stateless markup, and class components for anything with state, a lifecycle, or methods.

## Function components

A `FunctionComponent<AttrsType>` is a function from its attrs to what it renders. It receives its children as a second argument.

Function components must be idempotent with no side effects, and they do not support `mount()` and `unmount()`. Use a class component when you need either.

To accept children, add `ChildrenAttr` to the attrs type.

```tsx
import { type ChildrenAttr, type FunctionComponent, replaceElementWithRoot } from "@velotype/velotype"

type UserProfile = {
    name: string
    email?: string
    address?: string
}
type UserProfileAttrsType = {
    user: UserProfile
}

// A FunctionComponent takes attrs, and children as a second argument.
// It must be idempotent with no side effects, and it has no mount or unmount.
export const UserProfile: FunctionComponent<UserProfileAttrsType> = function(attrs: UserProfileAttrsType) {
    return <div>
        <div>Name: {attrs.user.name}</div>
        {attrs.user.email && <div>Email: {attrs.user.email}</div>}
        {attrs.user.address && <div>Address: {attrs.user.address}</div>}
    </div>
}

type PanelAttrsType = {title: string} & ChildrenAttr

export const Panel: FunctionComponent<PanelAttrsType> = function(attrs: PanelAttrsType, children) {
    return <section>
        <h2>{attrs.title}</h2>
        {children}
    </section>
}

replaceElementWithRoot(
    <Panel title="Profile">
        <UserProfile user={{name: "Ada", email: "ada@example.com"}}/>
    </Panel>,
    document.getElementById("app"),
)
```
## Class components

A class component extends `Component<AttrsType>` and implements `render()`. Velotype calls its lifecycle methods for you.

The attrs a Component is created with are `this.attrs`, and its children are `this.children`. They are also passed to `render()`.

A Component that accepts children adds `ChildrenAttr` to its attrs type.

```tsx
import { type ChildrenAttr, Component, type RenderableElements, replaceElementWithRoot } from "@velotype/velotype"

type GreetingAttrsType = {
    name: string
    punctuation?: string
}

// A Component is a class. Its attrs are the type parameter, and render() returns what it shows.
class Greeting extends Component<GreetingAttrsType> {
    override render(attrs: Readonly<GreetingAttrsType>) {
        return <div>Hello {attrs.name}{attrs.punctuation ?? "!"}</div>
    }
}

// A Component that accepts children adds ChildrenAttr to its attrs. The children it is created
// with are passed to render(), and are also this.children.
class Card extends Component<ChildrenAttr> {
    override render(_attrs: Readonly<ChildrenAttr>, children: RenderableElements[]) {
        return <div class="card">{children}</div>
    }
}

replaceElementWithRoot(
    <Card>
        <Greeting name="Ada"/>
        <Greeting name="Grace" punctuation="?"/>
    </Card>,
    document.getElementById("app"),
)
```
## The lifecycle

A Component goes through `mount()`, `render()`, and `unmount()`. A Component can also call `this.refresh()` to render again.

```tsx
import { type ChildrenAttr, Component, RenderBasic, type RenderableElements, replaceElementWithRoot } from "@velotype/velotype"

type MoreComplexAttrsType = {
    requiredAttr: string
    optionalAttr?: string
} & ChildrenAttr

class MoreComplexComponent extends Component<MoreComplexAttrsType> {
    renderCallCount: number = 0
    someMethodCallCount: number = 0
    otherMethodCallCount = new RenderBasic<number>(0)

    // Called once, just after the Component is inserted into the page, before the browser paints.
    // Child Components mount before their parent.
    override mount() {
        console.log("This component was just added to the DOM")
    }

    // Called once, just before the Component is removed, while it is still in the page
    override unmount() {
        console.log("This component is about to be removed from the DOM")
    }

    override render(attrs: Readonly<MoreComplexAttrsType>, children: RenderableElements[]) {
        this.renderCallCount++
        return <div>
            This is a more complex Component for {attrs.requiredAttr}
            <div>render() has been called: {this.renderCallCount} times</div>
            <button type="button" onClick={this.otherMethod}>click me (RenderBasic) {this.otherMethodCallCount}</button>
            <button type="button" onClick={this.someMethod}>click me (refresh) {this.someMethodCallCount}</button>
            <div>
                Children here:
                <div>{children}</div>
            </div>
        </div>
    }

    otherMethod = () => {
        // Updating the RenderBasic renders only the one {this.otherMethodCallCount} element above
        this.otherMethodCallCount.value += 1
    }

    someMethod = () => {
        this.someMethodCallCount += 1
        // A full render of this Component: its children are unmounted and deleted, then render()
        // runs again and creates and mounts a fresh set. This Component stays mounted.
        this.refresh()
    }
}

replaceElementWithRoot(
    <MoreComplexComponent requiredAttr="the docs"><span>a child</span></MoreComplexComponent>,
    document.getElementById("app"),
)
```
* `render()` creates the Component's elements. It can run again when the Component calls `refresh()`
* `mount()` runs just after the Component is inserted into the page, before the browser paints, so it can read layout (such as `getBoundingClientRect()`). Child Components mount before their parent. For work that should wait until after the first paint, start it from `mount()` with `requestAnimationFrame()` or `setTimeout()`
* `unmount()` runs just before the Component is removed, while it is still in the page
* `refresh()` unmounts and mounts the Component's children, and the Component itself stays mounted. If `render()` throws, the current render is kept and the error is thrown to the caller of `refresh()`
* Moving an element (such as `swap()`, or moving it with DOM methods) does not unmount or mount it
* A Component mounts and unmounts once. Once Velotype removes it, it is released, and inserting its element again does not mount it (Velotype warns in the console). Create a new Component instead
* Velotype mounts Components that are inserted through Velotype: `replaceElementWithRoot()`, a Component's child methods, and RenderObjects. An element inserted with DOM methods such as `appendChild()` is not mounted
* Likewise Velotype unmounts Components that are removed through Velotype: `removeElementRoot()`, a Component's child methods, `refresh()`, and RenderObjects. An element removed with DOM methods is not unmounted
* The RenderObjects in a Component's fields mount and unmount with it (calling their `registerOnMount()` callbacks), and the ones in public fields are released when it unmounts. To share a RenderObject between Components, pass it in attrs or keep it in a `#private` field
* Errors thrown by `mount()` and `unmount()` are reported with `reportError()`, and the other Components still run. See [Errors](/docs/velotype/events-and-errors/#when-code-throws)

### Prefer RenderObjects to refresh()

`refresh()` is the largest possible update: it throws away the Component's children and creates them again, which loses their state. To change part of a Component, use a [RenderObject](/docs/velotype/render-objects/) for a value, or a [child method](#changing-part-of-what-a-component-rendered) for an element.

## Cleaning up with unmountSignal

`this.unmountSignal` is an `AbortSignal` that is aborted just after `unmount()` returns. Pass it to what `mount()` starts, and it is cleaned up without an `unmount()`. It works with `addEventListener()` and with `fetch()`, so a response that arrives after the Component unmounts is not used.

The signal is created on first use. It is also aborted when a Component is released without being mounted, such as when its `render()` throws.

```tsx
import { Component, type EmptyAttrs, RenderBasic } from "@velotype/velotype"

// this.unmountSignal is aborted just after unmount() returns. Pass it to what mount() starts,
// and it is cleaned up without an unmount().
export class WindowWidth extends Component<EmptyAttrs> {
    width = new RenderBasic<number>(globalThis.innerWidth)

    override mount() {
        globalThis.addEventListener("resize", () => {
            this.width.value = globalThis.innerWidth
        }, {signal: this.unmountSignal})
    }

    override render() {
        return <div>Window width: {this.width}</div>
    }
}

// It works with fetch() too, so a response that arrives after the Component unmounts is not used
export class Greeting extends Component<EmptyAttrs> {
    message = new RenderBasic<string>("Loading")

    override mount() {
        fetch("/greeting", {signal: this.unmountSignal})
            .then(response => response.text())
            .then(text => { this.message.value = text })
            .catch(() => { /* aborted, or failed */ })
    }

    override render() {
        return <div>{this.message}</div>
    }
}
```
## Changing part of what a Component rendered

A Component's child methods change one element inside what it rendered, without a `refresh()`. Each takes an element from this Component's render, mounts what it inserts, and unmounts what it removes.

| Method | Does |
|---|---|
| `replaceChild(child, newChild)` | Replaces `child`, and returns the new element |
| `appendToChild(child, newChild)` | Adds `newChild` to the end of `child` |
| `prependToChild(child, newChild)` | Adds `newChild` to the start of `child` |
| `replaceChildrenOfChild(child, newChildren)` | Replaces all of `child`'s children |
| `removeChild(child)` | Removes `child` |

The methods return `false` (or `child`, for `replaceChild()`) and change nothing when `child` is not part of this Component's render.

```tsx
import { Component, type EmptyAttrs } from "@velotype/velotype"

// A Component's child methods change one element inside what it rendered, without a refresh().
// Each takes an element from this Component's render, mounts what it inserts, and unmounts what
// it removes.
export class Panel extends Component<EmptyAttrs> {
    body: HTMLElement = <div>Loading...</div>
    list: HTMLUListElement = <ul><li>second</li></ul>
    note: HTMLElement = <p>A note that is removed later</p>

    override mount() {
        fetch("/panel", {signal: this.unmountSignal}).then(response => response.text()).then(text => {
            // replaceChild() returns the new element
            this.body = this.replaceChild(this.body, <div>{text}</div>) as HTMLElement

            // add to the end or start of an element
            this.appendToChild(this.list, <li>third</li>)
            this.prependToChild(this.list, <li>first</li>)

            // replace all of an element's children
            this.replaceChildrenOfChild(this.list, [<li>one</li>, <li>two</li>])

            // remove an element. These return false (replaceChild() returns the child) and change
            // nothing when the element is not part of this Component's render.
            const removed: boolean = this.removeChild(this.note)
            console.log("removed", removed)
        })
    }

    override render() {
        return <section>
            {this.body}
            {this.list}
            {this.note}
        </section>
    }
}
```
## Getting the Component from its element

TSX evaluates to the element, but the TypeScript type of a tag for a class is the class. `getComponent<T>(element)` converts an element that was created for a class Component back to the instance, so you can call its methods.

```tsx
import { Component, type EmptyAttrs, getComponent } from "@velotype/velotype"

class AdvancedComponent extends Component<EmptyAttrs> {
    override render() {
        return <div>This is an advanced Component</div>
    }
    someMethod() {
        console.log("AdvancedComponent someMethod() called")
    }
}

// JSX evaluates to the element, and getComponent() converts it back to the instance that made it
const instance: AdvancedComponent = getComponent<AdvancedComponent>(<AdvancedComponent/>)
instance.someMethod()

// The element is still usable in TSX
const page = <div>{instance}</div>
document.body.append(page)
```
## Accepting id, class, and style

`passthroughAttrsToElement(element, attrs)` sets the `id`, `class`, and `style` attrs that a caller passed on the element a Component renders. `class` is added to the element's own classes rather than replacing them. Add `IdAttr` and `StylePassthroughAttrs` to the Component's attrs type to accept them.

`setAttrsOnElement(element, attrs)` sets attributes, style objects, and event listeners on an existing element the same way TSX does.

```tsx
import { Component, type IdAttr, passthroughAttrsToElement, setAttrsOnElement, type StylePassthroughAttrs } from "@velotype/velotype"

// IdAttr and StylePassthroughAttrs add id, class, and style to a Component's attrs
type ButtonAttrs = IdAttr & StylePassthroughAttrs & {label: string}

class FancyButton extends Component<ButtonAttrs> {
    override render(attrs: Readonly<ButtonAttrs>) {
        // Sets the id, class, and style the caller passed. class is added to the element's own
        // classes rather than replacing them.
        return passthroughAttrsToElement(<button type="button" class="fancy">{attrs.label}</button>, attrs)
    }
}

const button = <FancyButton label="Save" id="save" class="primary" style={{marginTop: "4px"}}/>

// setAttrsOnElement() sets attributes, style objects, and event listeners on an existing element
// the same way TSX does
const input = document.createElement("input")
setAttrsOnElement(input, {
    type: "text",
    class: "wide",
    style: {width: "100%"},
    onInput: () => console.log("typed"),
})

document.body.append(button, input)
```

---

Source: https://velotype.github.io/docs/velotype/render-objects/

# RenderObjects

A RenderObject holds a value and renders it to the page. When the value changes, every place it was rendered updates, and nothing else does. This is how Velotype updates the page in place, without a virtual DOM.

Create RenderObjects as fields of Component classes. Using them in any other way is advanced behavior.

## RenderObject

`new RenderObject<DataType>(initialValue, renderFunction)` holds a value and a function that renders a value into an element. Put the RenderObject in TSX as a child and it renders there. Put it in as many places as you like, and each one is rendered.

Setting `value` (or calling `set()`) renders the new value only when it is a different value (`!==`). `get()` and `value` read it.

```tsx
import { Component, type EmptyAttrs, RenderObject } from "@velotype/velotype"

type Person = {
    name: string
    address: string
    phone: string
}

class PersonSelector extends Component<EmptyAttrs> {
    // The first argument is the initial value, the second renders a value into an element
    selectedPerson = new RenderObject<Person | null>(null, function(person: Person | null) {
        if (!person) {
            return <div></div>
        } else {
            return <div>
                <div>Person:</div>
                <div>Name: {person.name}</div>
                <div>Address: {person.address}</div>
                <div>Phone: {person.phone}</div>
            </div>
        }
    })

    override render() {
        const people = [
            {name: "One person", address: "somewhere", phone: "123"},
            {name: "Two person", address: "elsewhere", phone: "456"},
            {name: "Three person", address: "nowhere", phone: "789"},
        ]
        return <div>
            {people.map((person) => <button type="button" onClick={() => {
                // Setting value renders the new value in both places below.
                // It renders only when the new value is a different value (!==).
                this.selectedPerson.value = person
            }}>{person.name}</button>)}
            <div>Render selected Person in one place: {this.selectedPerson}</div>
            <div>Render selected Person in another place: {this.selectedPerson}</div>
        </div>
    }
}

// get() and set() do the same as reading and writing value
const selector = new PersonSelector({}, [])
void selector

// When a value that is an object or Array is changed in place, render it again with rerenderElements()
class TagList extends Component<EmptyAttrs> {
    tags = new RenderObject<string[]>(["velotype"], (tags: string[]) => <ul>{tags.map(tag => <li>{tag}</li>)}</ul>)

    override render() {
        return <div>
            <button type="button" onClick={() => {
                const tags = this.tags.get()
                tags.push("tsx")
                this.tags.rerenderElements(tags)
            }}>Add a tag</button>
            {this.tags}
        </div>
    }
}
void TagList
```
When a value that is an object or an Array is changed in place, `!==` sees no change. Call `rerenderElements(value)` to render it again.

### Listening for changes

* `registerOnChangeListener(listener, options)` runs `listener` after each change of `value`
* `registerOnMount(onMount, onUnmount)` adds callbacks that run when the Component whose field holds the RenderObject mounts and unmounts

Both return the RenderObject, so they can be chained onto its creation. The options of `registerOnChangeListener()` are:

| Option | Does |
|---|---|
| `hasVtKey` | Removes the listener with this Component's lifecycle instead of the RenderObject's. It must already have a `vtKey`, so call it from the Component's `mount()` |
| `triggerOnRegistration` | Also runs the listener once, just after it is registered |
| `eventDispatchDelay` | Waits this many milliseconds before running the listener, and runs it at most once in that time |

```tsx
import { Component, type EmptyAttrs, RenderBasic, RenderObject } from "@velotype/velotype"

class Search extends Component<EmptyAttrs> {
    // Runs the listener after each change of value.
    // eventDispatchDelay waits that many milliseconds before running it, and runs it at most once
    // in that time, so it reads the latest value.
    query = new RenderBasic<string>("").registerOnChangeListener(() => {
        console.log("search for", this.query.value)
    }, {eventDispatchDelay: 250})

    // Callbacks that run when the Component whose field holds the RenderObject mounts and unmounts
    status = new RenderBasic<string>("idle").registerOnMount(
        () => console.log("mounted"),
        () => console.log("unmounted"),
    )

    // triggerOnRegistration also runs the listener once, just after it is registered
    log = new RenderObject<string[]>([], (lines: string[]) => <pre>{lines.join("\n")}</pre>)
        .registerOnChangeListener(() => console.log("log changed"), {triggerOnRegistration: true})

    override mount() {
        // hasVtKey removes the listener with this Component's lifecycle instead of the
        // RenderObject's. The Component has its vtKey by the time mount() runs.
        this.status.registerOnChangeListener(() => console.log("status is", this.status.value), {hasVtKey: this})
    }

    override render() {
        return <div>
            <input type="search" onInput={(event: Event) => this.query.value = (event.target as HTMLInputElement).value}/>
            <div>Status: {this.status}</div>
            {this.log}
        </div>
    }
}
void Search
```
### Updating in place with handleUpdate

By default a new value renders new elements. For elements that change often, return an `UpdateHandlerLink` from the render function with references to the parts that change, and pass a `handleUpdate` function as the third argument. It updates those parts in place instead. The second type parameter of RenderObject types the references.

```tsx
import { Component, type EmptyAttrs, RenderObject, UpdateHandlerLink } from "@velotype/velotype"

type Score = {player: string, points: number}
// The references the render function keeps for handleUpdate: the parts that change
type ScoreRefs = {points: HTMLElement}

class ScoreBoard extends Component<EmptyAttrs> {
    // By default a new value renders new elements. Return an UpdateHandlerLink from the render
    // function, with references to the parts that change, and pass a handleUpdate function that
    // changes those parts in place.
    score = new RenderObject<Score, ScoreRefs>({player: "Ada", points: 0}, (score: Score) => {
        const points = <span>{score.points}</span>
        return new UpdateHandlerLink(<div>{score.player}: {points}</div>, {points})
    }, (_element, refs, _oldScore, newScore) => {
        refs.points.textContent = String(newScore.points)
    })

    override render() {
        return <div>
            {this.score}
            <button type="button" onClick={() => {
                this.score.value = {player: this.score.value.player, points: this.score.value.points + 1}
            }}>Add a point</button>
        </div>
    }
}
void ScoreBoard
```
## RenderBasic

`RenderBasic<DataType>` is a RenderObject for a `string`, `number`, `bigint`, or `boolean`. It renders its value as text inside a `<span style="display:contents;">` and updates that text in place, so it needs no render function.

It adds `getString()` and `setString()`, which convert the value to and from a string.

```tsx
import { Component, type EmptyAttrs, RenderBasic } from "@velotype/velotype"

class Counter extends Component<EmptyAttrs> {
    // A RenderBasic holds a string, number, bigint, or boolean, and renders it as text inside a
    // <span style="display:contents;">, which it updates in place
    count = new RenderBasic<number>(0)

    override render() {
        return <div>
            <div>Counter value: {this.count}</div>
            <button type="button" onClick={() => this.count.value += 1}>Increment</button>
            <button type="button" onClick={() => this.count.value -= 1}>Decrement</button>
            <button type="button" onClick={() => this.count.setString("100")}>Set to 100</button>
            <button type="button" onClick={() => console.log(this.count.getString())}>Log it</button>
        </div>
    }
}
void Counter
```
## Other methods

| Method | Does |
|---|---|
| `getElements()` | The elements this RenderObject has rendered. Advanced: use carefully |
| `removeAll()` | Removes every element this RenderObject has rendered |
| `render(renderFunction, handleUpdate?)` | Renders one more element with a different render function than the default |

---

Source: https://velotype.github.io/docs/velotype/lists/

# Lists

Velotype has two list types. Both hold an Array of data points, and both render, move, and remove only the rows that changed. They have the same methods.

| | RenderObjectArray | RenderTemplateArray |
|---|---|---|
| A row is | rendered by TSX, by its own RenderObject | a clone of a template element, filled in with DOM APIs |
| Rows can hold | Components, RenderObjects, RenderBasics, and TSX event handlers | plain markup only |
| Row events | TSX handlers on elements in the row | `on`, one listener per event on the wrapper element |
| Fastest for | lists of rich rows | long or frequently rebuilt lists of plain rows |

Use RenderObjectArray when rows need Components, RenderObjects, or RenderBasics inside them, their own `mount()` and `unmount()`, or TSX event handlers. Use RenderTemplateArray for long or frequently rebuilt lists of plain markup, such as tables, logs, and search results, where each row is the same structure with a few changing values. In js-framework-benchmark it creates and replaces rows with about a quarter of the script time of RenderObjectArray, and clears rows in about half the time.

## RenderObjectArray

`new RenderObjectArray<DataType>({renderFunction})` renders each data point with its own RenderObject. The rows go into a wrapper element, which is a `<div style="display:contents;">` unless you pass `wrapperElementTag`. A named tag is created unstyled, and `wrapperAttrs` sets attributes on it.

```tsx
import { Component, type EmptyAttrs, RenderBasic, RenderObjectArray } from "@velotype/velotype"

type Todo = {
    text: string
}

class TodoList extends Component<EmptyAttrs> {
    // Each row is rendered by its own RenderObject, so a row can hold Components and RenderObjects,
    // and use TSX event handlers
    todos: RenderObjectArray<Todo> = new RenderObjectArray<Todo>({
        wrapperElementTag: "ul",
        renderFunction: (todo: Todo) => {
            const done = new RenderBasic<string>("")
            return <li>
                {todo.text}{done}
                <button type="button" onClick={() => done.value = " (done)"}>Done</button>
                <button type="button" onClick={() => this.todos.delete(todo)}>Remove</button>
            </li>
        },
    })
    textInput: HTMLInputElement = <input/>

    addTodo = () => {
        this.todos.push({text: this.textInput.value})
        this.textInput.value = ""
    }

    override render() {
        return <form onSubmit={this.addTodo} action="javascript:">
            <label>
                <span>Add Todo</span>
                {this.textInput}
            </label>
            <button type="submit">Add</button>
            {this.todos}
        </form>
    }
}
void TodoList
```
The options are `wrapperElementTag`, `wrapperAttrs`, `renderFunction`, and `handleUpdate` (the same advanced update function as [RenderObject](/docs/velotype/render-objects/#updating-in-place-with-handleupdate)).

## RenderTemplateArray

`new RenderTemplateArray<DataType, UpdateRefsType>({template, renderFunction})` builds a template element once, and every row is a `cloneNode()` of it that `renderFunction` fills in. It has no per-row bookkeeping to do when rows are created, updated, or removed, which is why it is fast.

```tsx
import { Component, type EmptyAttrs, RenderTemplateArray } from "@velotype/velotype"

type Server = {
    name: string
    cpu: number
}

class ServerList extends Component<EmptyAttrs> {
    // Rows are clones of the template. renderFunction fills in each new clone with DOM APIs.
    servers = new RenderTemplateArray<Server, null>({
        wrapperElementTag: "ul",
        template: <li></li>,
        renderFunction: (row: HTMLElement, server: Server) => {
            row.textContent = `${server.name} ${server.cpu}%`
            return null
        },
    })

    override mount() {
        this.servers.pushAll([
            {name: "eu-west-1", cpu: 40},
            {name: "us-east-1", cpu: 75},
            {name: "ap-south-1", cpu: 12},
        ])
    }

    override render() {
        return <div>
            <input type="search" placeholder="Filter" onInput={(event) => {
                const text = (event.target as HTMLInputElement).value
                // Rows that do not match are taken out of the page. filter(undefined) shows them all again.
                this.servers.filter(text === "" ? undefined : server => server.name.includes(text))
            }}/>
            <button type="button" onClick={() => this.servers.sort((a, b) => b.cpu - a.cpu)}>Busiest first</button>
            <button type="button" onClick={() => this.servers.move(this.servers.length - 1, 0)}>Last to top</button>
            {this.servers}
        </div>
    }
}
void ServerList
```
### Rules for templates

* The template must not contain Components, RenderObjects, or event listeners. `cloneNode()` does not copy event listeners
* Listen for row events with `on`, which adds one listener per event to the wrapper element and calls it with the event, the row element, its data, and its index. Only events that bubble can be listened for (use `focusin` and `focusout` instead of `focus` and `blur`)
* `renderFunction` fills in a new clone with DOM APIs and returns the references that `handleUpdate` needs
* `setAt()` calls `handleUpdate` to update a row in place. Without `handleUpdate`, the row is replaced with a new clone

```tsx
import { Component, type EmptyAttrs, RenderTemplateArray } from "@velotype/velotype"

type Row = {
    id: number
    label: string
}
// What renderFunction returns, and handleUpdate receives: the parts that change
type RowRefs = {
    label: Text
}

class RowTable extends Component<EmptyAttrs> {
    #nextId = 1

    rows: RenderTemplateArray<Row, RowRefs> = new RenderTemplateArray<Row, RowRefs>({
        wrapperElementTag: "tbody",
        // Built once, then cloned for every row. It must not hold Components, RenderObjects, or event listeners.
        template: <tr><td class="id"></td><td class="label"></td><td><button type="button" class="remove">Remove</button></td></tr>,
        // Fill in a new clone, and return the references that handleUpdate needs
        renderFunction: (row: HTMLElement, data: Row) => {
            row.children[0].textContent = String(data.id)
            const label = document.createTextNode(data.label)
            row.children[1].appendChild(label)
            return {label}
        },
        // Update a row in place when setAt() changes its data. Without it, setAt() replaces the row with a new clone.
        handleUpdate: (_row, refs, _oldData, newData) => {
            refs.label.data = newData.label
        },
        // One listener per event, on the wrapper element, called with the row, its data, and its index.
        // Only events that bubble can be listened for.
        on: {
            click: (event, _row, _data, index) => {
                if ((event.target as HTMLElement).closest(".remove")) {
                    this.rows.deleteAt(index)
                }
            },
        },
    })

    override render() {
        return <div>
            <button type="button" onClick={() => this.rows.push({id: this.#nextId++, label: "New row"})}>Add row</button>
            <button type="button" onClick={() => {
                if (this.rows.length > 0) {
                    this.rows.setAt(0, {id: this.rows.getAt(0).id, label: "Renamed row"})
                }
            }}>Rename first row</button>
            <button type="button" onClick={() => this.rows.swap(0, 1)}>Swap first two rows</button>
            <button type="button" onClick={() => this.rows.clear()}>Clear</button>
            <table>{this.rows}</table>
        </div>
    }
}
void RowTable
```
The options are `wrapperElementTag`, `wrapperAttrs`, `template`, `renderFunction`, `handleUpdate`, and `on`.

## Changing the Array

Every method changes the data and the page together.

| Method | Does |
|---|---|
| `push(data)` | Adds one data point to the end |
| `pushAll(data[])` | Adds several data points to the end |
| `insertAt(index, data)` | Inserts one data point before the data point at `index` |
| `insertAllAt(index, data[])` | Inserts several data points, in order, before the data point at `index` |
| `deleteAt(startIndex, deleteCount?)` | Removes the data point at `startIndex`, or `deleteCount` of them |
| `delete(data)` | Removes the first data point that is `data`, in linear time |
| `getAt(index)` | Reads the data point at `index` |
| `setAt(index, data)` | Replaces the data point at `index` |
| `swap(indexA, indexB)` | Swaps two data points and their rows |
| `move(from, to)` | Moves a data point so that it ends up at index `to` |
| `sort(compareFn)` | Sorts the data points, stably |
| `reorder(indexes)` | Puts the data points in any new order |
| `filter(predicate?)` | Shows only the data points that match |
| `clear()` | Removes every data point |
| `length` | The number of data points |

`insertAt()` and `insertAllAt()` are separate methods so that a data point can itself be an Array. Their `index` runs from `0` to `length`, or counts from the end when negative, as `Array.splice()` does.

```tsx
import { RenderObjectArray, RenderTemplateArray } from "@velotype/velotype"

// RenderObjectArray and RenderTemplateArray have the same methods.
// Only the rows that are affected are rendered, moved, or removed.
const letters = new RenderObjectArray<string>({
    wrapperElementTag: "ul",
    renderFunction: (letter: string) => <li>{letter}</li>,
})
const wrapper = <div>{letters}</div>
document.body.append(wrapper)

letters.push("b")                     // b
letters.pushAll(["c", "d"])           // b c d
letters.insertAt(0, "a")              // a b c d
letters.insertAllAt(4, ["e", "f"])    // a b c d e f
letters.insertAt(-1, "x")             // a b c d e x f   (negative counts from the end, as Array.splice() does)

console.log(letters.length)           // 7
console.log(letters.getAt(2))         // "c"

letters.setAt(5, "e2")                // a b c d e e2 f   (replaces the data point at an index)
letters.delete("e2")                  // a b c d e f      (removes the first data point that is this value)
letters.deleteAt(5)                   // a b c d e        (removes the data point at an index)
letters.deleteAt(0, 2)                // c d e            (removes 2 data points from index 0)

letters.swap(0, 1)                    // d c e
letters.move(0, 2)                    // c e d            (the moved data point ends up at index 2)

// sort() is stable, and moves only the rows that change places
letters.sort((a, b) => a.localeCompare(b))
```
