```tsx
// reorder() puts the data points in any order: afterwards the data point at index k is the one
// that was at indexes[k]. It throws a RangeError unless indexes holds each index once.
const count = letters.length
letters.reorder(Array.from({length: count}, (_, index) => count - 1 - index))

// filter() takes the rows that do not match out of the page, and filter(undefined) shows them all
// again. Indexes and length still count every data point.
letters.filter(letter => letter !== "d")
letters.filter(undefined)

letters.clear()

// A RenderTemplateArray is used the same way
const numbers = new RenderTemplateArray<number, null>({
    wrapperElementTag: "ol",
    template: <li></li>,
    renderFunction: (row: HTMLElement, value: number) => {
        row.textContent = String(value)
        return null
    },
})
numbers.pushAll([3, 1, 2])
numbers.sort((a, b) => a - b)
document.body.append(<div>{numbers}</div>)
```
### Sorting, moving, and filtering

These change the order of the rows, or which rows are shown, by moving the rows that are already rendered. They never render them again.

* `sort(compareFn)` sorts the data points as `Array.sort()` does, and it is stable. Only the rows that change places are moved, so re-sorting a list that is nearly in order, such as a table sorted by a column that a few `setAt()` calls changed, moves only those rows
* `reorder(indexes)` puts the data points in any new order: afterwards the data point at index `k` is the one that was at `indexes[k]`. It throws a `RangeError` unless `indexes` holds each index from `0` to `length - 1` once. Like `sort()`, it moves only the rows that change places
* `move(from, to)` moves one data point and its rows, so that it ends up at index `to`, as removing it with `splice(from, 1)` and inserting it with `splice(to, 0, data)` would
* `filter(predicate)` shows only the data points that `predicate` returns true for, and `filter(undefined)` shows them all again

When a filter is set, the other data points stay in the Array with their rows kept out of the page, so showing them again moves those rows back. Indexes, in `getAt()`, `setAt()`, `swap()`, the `on` listeners of a RenderTemplateArray, and the rest, still count every data point, and `length` is the length of the whole Array.

The predicate is applied to data points added later, and to one changed with `setAt()`. Call `filter()` again when what it tests for has changed, such as the text in a search box.

In a RenderObjectArray, the Components in a row that is filtered out stay mounted while it is out of the page, and a row added while filtered out mounts when it is first shown.

Taking rows out of the page is faster than hiding them with `hidden` or `display: none`: the browser does less work for each change when a list has fewer rows, and showing them again is faster than rendering them again.

## Very long lists

An update renders only the rows that changed, but one update that renders thousands of rows is still slow. Use RenderTemplateArray for the rows, and add them in batches, giving the browser a chance to paint and handle input between batches. `insertAllAt()` does the same at a position other than the end.

```tsx
import { Component, type EmptyAttrs, RenderTemplateArray } from "@velotype/velotype"

// Add thousands of rows in batches, giving the browser a chance to paint and handle input between batches
export async function pushInBatches<DataType>(array: {pushAll(data: DataType[]): void}, data: DataType[], batchSize = 1000) {
    for (let index = 0; index < data.length; index += batchSize) {
        array.pushAll(data.slice(index, index + batchSize))
        // Let the browser paint and handle input before the next batch
        await new Promise((resolve) => setTimeout(resolve, 0))
    }
}

class BigList extends Component<EmptyAttrs> {
    rows = new RenderTemplateArray<number, null>({
        wrapperElementTag: "ul",
        template: <li></li>,
        renderFunction: (row: HTMLElement, value: number) => {
            row.textContent = `Row ${value}`
            return null
        },
    })

    override mount() {
        pushInBatches(this.rows, Array.from({length: 10000}, (_, index) => index))
    }

    override render() {
        return <div>{this.rows}</div>
    }
}
void BigList
```
Where it is supported, `await scheduler.yield()` instead of `setTimeout()` resumes sooner after the browser has handled input. Work that is slow without rendering anything, such as parsing or sorting a large data set, belongs in a Web Worker.

---

Source: https://velotype.github.io/docs/velotype/async-data/

# Async data

`AsyncRenderObject` is a RenderObject for data that arrives later. It shows `pending()` while a Promise is loading, then `render()` with its result, or `onFail()` when the Promise rejects.

It is in its own module, so bundles that do not use it do not include it.

## Loading a value

Pass a Promise, or a function that gets an `AbortSignal` and returns one. Pass the function form when the load can be cancelled, as `fetch()` can.

```tsx
import { AsyncRenderObject, Component } from "@velotype/velotype"

type User = {name: string}

class UserCard extends Component<{id: string}> {
    // The first argument is a Promise, or a function that gets an AbortSignal and returns one
    user = new AsyncRenderObject<User>((signal) => fetch(`/users/${this.attrs.id}`, {signal}).then(response => response.json()), {
        pending: () => <p>Loading</p>,
        render: (user: User) => <p>{user.name}</p>,
        onFail: () => <p>Could not load the user</p>,
        // Keep showing the resolved value while load() fetches a new one
        keepPrevious: true,
    })

    override render() {
        return <div>
            {this.user}
            <button type="button" onClick={() => {
                // Replaces the load in progress, so only the latest load is shown
                this.user.load((signal) => fetch(`/users/${this.attrs.id}`, {signal}).then(response => response.json()))
            }}>Reload</button>
            <button type="button" onClick={() => {
                // Show a state directly, such as a value that is already known. This cancels the load in progress.
                this.user.set({status: "resolved", value: {name: "Ada"}})
            }}>Use a known user</button>
            <div>{this.user.loading ? "Loading..." : "Idle"}</div>
        </div>
    }
}
void UserCard
```
The options are:

| Option | Does |
|---|---|
| `render(value)` | Renders the resolved value. Required |
| `pending()` | Renders what is shown while loading. The default is a hidden element |
| `onFail(reason)` | Renders what is shown when loading rejects, or when `render()` throws |
| `keepPrevious` | Keeps showing the resolved value while `load()` fetches a new one, instead of showing `pending()` again |

## How it behaves

* **Only the latest load is shown.** `load()` replaces the load in progress, so a slower, earlier request that finishes last does not overwrite a newer one
* **Loads are cancelled** when a newer `load()` or `set()` replaces them, and when the AsyncRenderObject unmounts (as a field of a Component, when that Component unmounts). The function's `AbortSignal` is aborted and the result is ignored
* **`keepPrevious: true`** keeps showing the resolved value while `load()` fetches a new one. `loading` is `true` while a load is in progress
* **Errors:** a rejection, or a `render()` that throws, shows `onFail(reason)`. Without `onFail`, the error is reported with `reportError()` and a hidden element is shown
* `value` is the current state: `{status: "pending"}`, `{status: "resolved", value}`, or `{status: "rejected", reason}`
* `set(state)` shows a state directly, such as a value that is already known, and cancels the load in progress
* `pending()` is shown first even when the Promise has already resolved, since a Promise's result is only available asynchronously

## Loading code on demand

The same pattern loads code when it is needed, such as a Component that is only used after a click. To show several loads at once, load `Promise.all()` of them into one AsyncRenderObject.

```tsx
import { AsyncRenderObject, Component, type EmptyAttrs } from "@velotype/velotype"

// Loading code on demand: a Component that is only needed after a click
class LazyChart extends Component<EmptyAttrs> {
    chart = new AsyncRenderObject(import("./chart-module.tsx"), {
        pending: () => <p>Loading chart</p>,
        render: (module) => <module.Chart/>,
    })

    override render() {
        return <div>{this.chart}</div>
    }
}

// To show several loads at once, load Promise.all() of them into one AsyncRenderObject
class Dashboard extends Component<EmptyAttrs> {
    data = new AsyncRenderObject(Promise.all([
        fetch("/users").then(response => response.json() as Promise<string[]>),
        fetch("/teams").then(response => response.json() as Promise<string[]>),
    ]), {
        render: ([users, teams]) => <p>{users.length} users on {teams.length} teams</p>,
    })

    override render() {
        return <div>{this.data}</div>
    }
}
void LazyChart
void Dashboard
```
## Keeping the page responsive

An update renders only the RenderObject or rows whose value changed, so most updates are small and finish within a frame. Velotype has no scheduler to make them interruptible, so updates are slow in two cases: when frequent input, such as typing, starts expensive work each time, and when one update renders thousands of elements.

For frequent input, run the expensive work from a listener with `eventDispatchDelay`, so it runs at most once in that time instead of once per change. The listener runs after the delay, so it reads the latest `value`. Here a search runs at most every 250ms while typing, and the AsyncRenderObject shows only the latest search's results and aborts the earlier requests:

```tsx
import { AsyncRenderObject, Component, type EmptyAttrs, RenderBasic } from "@velotype/velotype"

type Result = {title: string}

class Search extends Component<EmptyAttrs> {
    // Shows only the latest search's results, and aborts the earlier requests
    results = new AsyncRenderObject<Result[]>(Promise.resolve([]), {
        render: (results) => <ul>{results.map((result) => <li>{result.title}</li>)}</ul>,
        keepPrevious: true,
    })

    // The listener runs at most once every 250ms while typing, and reads the latest value
    query = new RenderBasic<string>("").registerOnChangeListener(() => {
        const query = this.query.value
        this.results.load((signal) => fetch(`/search?q=${encodeURIComponent(query)}`, {signal}).then(response => response.json()))
    }, {eventDispatchDelay: 250})

    override render() {
        return <div>
            <input type="search" onInput={(event: Event) => this.query.value = (event.target as HTMLInputElement).value}/>
            {this.results}
        </div>
    }
}
void Search
```
For thousands of rows, see [very long lists](/docs/velotype/lists/#very-long-lists).

---

Source: https://velotype.github.io/docs/velotype/styling-and-raw-html/

# Styling and raw HTML

## Stylesheets

`setStylesheet(css, key, reset = false)` adds a stylesheet to the page, using `document.adoptedStyleSheets`, once per `key`. Call it from a Component's constructor or `render()` every time, and it adds no duplicates.

By default a key that is already added is left alone. Pass `true` as the third argument to replace the stylesheet already added under `key`.

```tsx
import { Component, type EmptyAttrs, type RenderableElements, setStylesheet } from "@velotype/velotype"

class Card extends Component<EmptyAttrs> {
    constructor(attrs: EmptyAttrs, children: RenderableElements[]) {
        super(attrs, children)
        // Adds the stylesheet to the page once per key, so calling this for every Card does not add duplicates
        setStylesheet(`.card { padding: 8px; border-radius: 4px; }`, "card")
    }

    override render() {
        return <div class="card">{this.children}</div>
    }
}

// Pass true as the third argument to replace the stylesheet already added under the key
setStylesheet(`.card { padding: 16px; border-radius: 8px; }`, "card", true)
void Card
```
In development, with the `jsx-dev-runtime`, `setStylesheet()` replaces a sheet whose text has changed, so styles update when their module runs again.

## Inline styles

The `style` attribute takes an object. See [style objects](/docs/velotype/#style-objects) for what is checked.

## Raw HTML, SVG, and MathML

Velotype creates TSX tags as HTML elements, so SVG and MathML content is added with the `SVG` and `MATH` Components. They set a string of markup as the `innerHTML` of an `<svg>` or `<math>` element. `HTML` does the same on any HTML tag, which is a `<div>` unless you pass `tag`.

The markup is not escaped, so only use content that is known to be safe.

```tsx
import { HTML, MATH, SVG } from "@velotype/velotype"

// SVG and MathML content is added with the SVG and MATH Components, which set a string of markup
// as the innerHTML of an <svg> or <math> element. HTML does the same on any HTML tag (a <div> by default).
// The markup is not escaped, so only use content that is known to be safe.
const icon = <SVG innerHTML={`<path d="M2 2 L10 10"/>`} elementAttrs={{viewBox: "0 0 12 12", width: "12", height: "12"}}/>
const formula = <MATH innerHTML="<mi>x</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>2</mn>"/>
const snippet = <HTML tag="p" innerHTML="Some <b>bold</b> text"/>

document.body.append(icon, formula, snippet)
```
| Component | Attrs |
|---|---|
| `HTML` | `innerHTML`, `tag` (default `div`), and `elementAttrs` for the element's attributes |
| `SVG` | `innerHTML`, and `elementAttrs` for the `<svg>` element's attributes |
| `MATH` | `innerHTML`, and `elementAttrs` for the `<math>` element's attributes |

---

Source: https://velotype.github.io/docs/velotype/events-and-errors/

# Events and errors

## The event bus

The event bus sends an event to every listener registered for a key, without the sender and receiver knowing about each other.

* `registerEventListener(component, key, listener)` registers `listener` for the events sent under `key`
* `emitEvent(key, event, emitter?)` sends a `VelotypeEvent` to the listeners of `key`. Passing the emitting Component as the third argument skips that Component's own listeners
* `removeEventListeners(component, key, listener?)` removes one listener, or every listener of `key` for that Component when no listener is passed

Listeners are removed automatically when the Component they were registered for unmounts.

A `VelotypeEvent` has `emittingObject`, `event` (a name), and `data`.

Register a Component's listeners in `mount()`. A Component gets its `vtKey`, which the listener is registered under, after its constructor returns, so `registerEventListener()` throws a `TypeError` when called from a constructor or a field initializer.

```tsx
import { Component, type EmptyAttrs, emitEvent, RenderBasic, registerEventListener, removeEventListeners, VelotypeEvent } from "@velotype/velotype"

class Status extends Component<EmptyAttrs> {
    message = new RenderBasic<string>("")

    private onStatus = (event: VelotypeEvent) => {
        this.message.value = String(event.data)
    }

    // Register a Component's listeners in mount(). A Component gets its vtKey after its constructor
    // returns, so registerEventListener() throws a TypeError when called from a constructor or a
    // field initializer. Listeners are removed when the Component unmounts.
    override mount() {
        registerEventListener(this, "status", this.onStatus)
    }

    stopListening() {
        // Remove one listener, or every listener for the key when no listener is passed
        removeEventListeners(this, "status", this.onStatus)
    }

    override render() {
        return <div>{this.message}</div>
    }
}

class Saver extends Component<EmptyAttrs> {
    override render() {
        return <button type="button" onClick={() => {
            // Sends the event to every listener of "status". Passing the emitting Component as the
            // third argument skips that Component's own listeners.
            emitEvent("status", new VelotypeEvent(this, "saved", "Saved"), this)
        }}>Save</button>
    }
}
void Status
void Saver
```
## When code throws

Velotype keeps its own state consistent whatever an app's code throws.

* **Errors in rendering are thrown to the caller:** a Component's constructor or `render()`, a function component, and a RenderObject's render function or `handleUpdate`. What the failed render created is released. `refresh()` keeps the current render, a RenderObject keeps its current value, and RenderObjectArray and RenderTemplateArray keep their data and rows matching
* **Errors in `mount()`, `unmount()`, `registerOnMount()` callbacks, and event bus listeners are reported** with `reportError()`, which logs them and dispatches an `error` event on the window. The other Components and listeners still run
* **An [AsyncRenderObject](/docs/velotype/async-data/) shows `onFail()`** when its Promise rejects or its `render()` throws, and reports the error with `reportError()` when it has no `onFail()`

A `handleUpdate` changes elements in place, so one that throws partway leaves its own elements partly updated.

## ErrorBoundary

To show a fallback instead of throwing, extend `ErrorBoundary` and implement `renderContent()` and `renderError()`. When `renderContent()` throws, on first render or on `refresh()`, what it created is released and `renderError()` is rendered instead.

```tsx
import { Component, type EmptyAttrs, ErrorBoundary } from "@velotype/velotype"

class Chart extends Component<EmptyAttrs> {
    override render(): HTMLElement {
        throw new Error("The chart data is missing")
    }
}

// When renderContent() throws, on first render or on refresh(), what it created is released and
// renderError() is rendered instead
class SafeChart extends ErrorBoundary<EmptyAttrs> {
    override renderContent() {
        // Create the Components to protect here. A Component passed in as a child is created by the
        // parent before the ErrorBoundary, so its errors are not caught.
        return <div><Chart/></div>
    }

    override renderError(error: unknown) {
        return <div>The chart could not be shown: {String(error)}</div>
    }
}

document.body.append(<SafeChart/>)
```
An ErrorBoundary catches errors from the Components that `renderContent()` creates, but not from its children: in `<SafeChart><Chart/></SafeChart>` the `Chart` is created by the parent before `SafeChart`, so create the Components to protect inside `renderContent()`. It also does not catch errors from event handlers or later RenderObject updates. An error thrown by `renderError()` is thrown to the code that created or refreshed the ErrorBoundary.

---

Source: https://velotype.github.io/docs/velotype/server-rendering/

# Server rendering

Velotype renders in the browser. To send a page's HTML from the server, render it with [velossr](/docs/velossr/), the server-side version of Velotype. It has its own components built for rendering on the server: static parts are prepared once, and async parts are streamed.

## No hydration step

There is no hydration step that turns the server's HTML into live Velotype Components. Velotype creates elements as TSX runs, so the interactive parts of a page are rendered again in the browser, and each one replaces the server's HTML for it with `replaceElementWithRoot()`. Rendering again is fast, the swap happens in one step when the page's script runs, and the server's HTML is shown until then.

This is the island pattern:

1. The server renders the markup for each interactive part (an island), and the data its Component is created with, as JSON in a `<script type="application/json">`
2. The browser creates each island's Component from its data and swaps it in, keeping what the user typed into the server's form fields before the script ran

The server half is in the [velossr docs](/docs/velossr/). This is the browser half:

```tsx
import { Component, RenderBasic, replaceElementWithRoot } from "@velotype/velotype"

type CounterData = {start: number, label: string}

class Counter extends Component<CounterData> {
    count = new RenderBasic<number>(this.attrs.start)

    override render(attrs: Readonly<CounterData>) {
        return <div class="counter">
            <span>{attrs.label}: {this.count}</span>
            <input name="note"/>
            <button type="button" onClick={() => { this.count.value += 1 }}>+1</button>
        </div>
    }
}

/** Replace the server-rendered island id with the element that render creates from the island's data */
function hydrate<DataType>(id: string, render: (data: DataType) => HTMLElement): void {
    const serverElement = document.getElementById(id)
    const dataElement = document.getElementById(id + "-data")
    if (!serverElement || !dataElement) {
        return
    }
    const element = render(JSON.parse(dataElement.textContent || "null"))
    // Keep what the user typed or picked before this script ran, pairing form fields by their order
    const fields = "input, textarea, select"
    const serverFields = serverElement.querySelectorAll<HTMLInputElement>(fields)
    const newFields = element.querySelectorAll<HTMLInputElement>(fields)
    let focused: HTMLElement | null = null
    for (let i = 0; i < serverFields.length && i < newFields.length; i++) {
        newFields[i].value = serverFields[i].value
        newFields[i].checked = serverFields[i].checked
        if (serverFields[i] === document.activeElement) {
            focused = newFields[i]
        }
    }
    replaceElementWithRoot(element, serverElement)
    if (focused) {
        focused.focus()
    }
}

hydrate<CounterData>("counter", data => <Counter {...data}/>)
```
* Keep the server's markup and the Component's render the same structure, so that nothing moves when the island is replaced
* The server and browser files use different JSX settings (`"jsxImportSource": "@velotype/velossr"` and `"@velotype/velotype"`), so keep them in separate directories with their own `deno.json`, or set it per file with a `/** @jsxImportSource @velotype/velossr */` comment

---

Source: https://velotype.github.io/docs/velotype/development-tools/

# Development tools

## Hot reloading

The `jsx-dev-runtime` entry point (used by the `react-jsxdev` JSX transform) supports hot updates. When a development server runs changed code again, the Components on the page are updated in place and keep their state. The `jsx-runtime` entry point used in production builds does not include any of it.

The [veloserver](/docs/veloserver/) development server (`@velotype/veloserver/dev`) provides two hot update modes:

* `module`: each module is served unbundled, and only the changed modules run again
* `bundle`: the app bundle is rebuilt and runs again

What happens when code changes:

* When a class Component changes, its live instances get the new methods and render again with their fields kept
* When a function Component changes, its output is rendered again in place
* Changes to constructors and field initializers apply to new instances only
* A class with `#private` members is replaced with a new instance, losing its state
* The child Components of a Component that renders again are created again

The development server talks to the dev runtime through `globalThis.__VELOTYPE_HOT__`, and other development servers can use it too.

## Debugging

The [Velotype DevTools](/docs/velotype/devtools/) extension shows the live component tree, the event bus and a trace of its events, and VSON payloads.

`@velotype/velotype/devtools` exports read-only access to Velotype's internal state (`__vtAppMetadata`) and the devtools hook (`getDevtoolsHook()`), for debugging and for the extension. Applications do not need to import it, because Velotype registers with the devtools hook from any entry point.

From Velotype 0.3.2, `__vtAppMetadata.setEventTracer(tracer)` calls `tracer(listeningKey, event)` once for each event that has listeners, just before the first listener receives it, and `setEventTracer(undefined)` stops. Tracing wraps the registered listeners, so emitting an event runs the same code whether or not anything is tracing. A tracer that throws does not affect the event or its listeners.

```tsx
// Read-only access to Velotype's internal state, for debugging and for the Velotype DevTools
// extension. Applications do not need it: Velotype registers with the devtools hook from any entry point.
import { __vtAppMetadata, getDevtoolsHook } from "@velotype/velotype/devtools"

console.log(__vtAppMetadata)
console.log(getDevtoolsHook())
```

---

Source: https://velotype.github.io/docs/velotype/api-reference/

# API reference

Everything `@velotype/velotype` exports, by area. Types are shown as they appear in the package. Each name links to the guide that covers it with an example.

## Mounting

| Export | Signature |
|---|---|
| [`replaceElementWithRoot`](/docs/velotype/#mounting-an-app) | `(rootComponent: AnchorElement, element: HTMLElement \| null) => AnchorElement \| null` |
| [`removeElementRoot`](/docs/velotype/#mounting-an-app) | `(element: AnchorElement \| null) => void` |

## Components

### Component

`abstract class Component<AttrsType> implements HasVtKey`

| Member | Description |
|---|---|
| `constructor(attrs: Readonly<AttrsType>, children: RenderableElements[])` | Receives the attrs and children. Rarely overridden |
| `readonly attrs: AttrsType` | The attrs the Component was created with |
| `readonly children: RenderableElements[]` | The children the Component was created with |
| `readonly vtKey: number` | A unique key per instance. Set after the constructor returns, so it is undefined in the constructor and in field initializers |
| `protected render(attrs, children): RenderableElements` | Abstract. Renders the Component |
| `protected mount(): void` | Called once, just after the Component is inserted, before the browser paints |
| `protected unmount(): void` | Called once, just before the Component is removed |
| `get refresh(): () => void` | Renders the Component's children again |
| `get unmountSignal(): AbortSignal` | Aborted just after `unmount()` returns |
| `get replaceChild(): (child, newChild) => AnchorElement` | Replaces one element of this Component's render |
| `get appendToChild(): (child, newChild) => boolean` | Adds to the end of an element |
| `get prependToChild(): (child, newChild) => boolean` | Adds to the start of an element |
| `get replaceChildrenOfChild(): (child, newChildren) => boolean` | Replaces all of an element's children |
| `get removeChild(): (child) => boolean` | Removes an element |

See [Components](/docs/velotype/components/).

### ErrorBoundary

`abstract class ErrorBoundary<AttrsType> extends Component<AttrsType>`

| Member | Description |
|---|---|
| `protected renderContent(attrs, children): RenderableElements` | Abstract. Renders the content |
| `protected renderError(error: unknown, attrs, children): RenderableElements` | Abstract. Renders the fallback when `renderContent()` throws |

See [Events and errors](/docs/velotype/events-and-errors/#errorboundary).

### Other

| Export | Description |
|---|---|
| `getComponent<T>(element)` | Converts an element created for a class Component back to the instance |
| `passthroughAttrsToElement(element, attrs)` | Sets the `id`, `class`, and `style` attrs on the element a Component renders |
| `setAttrsOnElement(element, attrs?)` | Sets attributes, style objects, and event listeners on an existing element |
| `createElement(tag, attrs, ...children)` | What TSX compiles tags to in the classic runtime |
| `createFragment(attrs, ...children)` | What `<>...</>` compiles to |
| `jsx`, `jsxs`, `Fragment` | The automatic JSX runtime |

## RenderObjects

### RenderObject

`class RenderObject<DataType, UpdateRefsType = any> implements HasVtKey`

| Member | Description |
|---|---|
| `constructor(initialData, defaultRenderFunction?, defaultHandleUpdate?)` | Creates a RenderObject |
| `value` | Reads or sets the value |
| `get(): DataType` | Reads the value |
| `set(newData: DataType): void` | Sets the value, and renders it if it is a different value |
| `rerenderElements(newData: DataType): void` | Sets the value and renders it again, even if it is the same object |
| `registerOnChangeListener(listener, options?): this` | Runs `listener` after each change. Options: `hasVtKey`, `triggerOnRegistration`, `eventDispatchDelay` |
| `registerOnMount(onMount?, onUnmount?): this` | Runs callbacks when the owning Component mounts and unmounts |
| `render(renderFunction, handleUpdate?): AnchorElement` | Renders one more element with another render function |
| `getElements(): AnchorElement[]` | The rendered elements. Advanced |
| `removeAll(): void` | Removes every rendered element |
| `readonly vtKey: number` | This RenderObject's key |

See [RenderObjects](/docs/velotype/render-objects/).

### RenderBasic

`class RenderBasic<DataType extends BasicTypes> extends RenderObject<DataType, Text>`

| Member | Description |
|---|---|
| `constructor(initialData: DataType)` | Creates a RenderBasic |
| `getString(): string` | The value as a string |
| `setString(newDataString: string): void` | Sets the value from a string |

### UpdateHandlerLink

`class UpdateHandlerLink<UpdateRefsType = any>`

`constructor(result: RenderableElements, updateRefs: UpdateRefsType)`, with `readonly result` and `readonly updateRefs`. Returned from a render function to give `handleUpdate` its references.

### AsyncRenderObject

`class AsyncRenderObject<DataType> extends RenderObject<AsyncState<DataType>>`

| Member | Description |
|---|---|
| `constructor(source: AsyncSource<DataType>, options: AsyncRenderObjectOptions<DataType>)` | Starts loading `source` |
| `load(source: AsyncSource<DataType>): void` | Replaces the load in progress |
| `get loading(): boolean` | `true` while a load is in progress |

```ts
type AsyncSource<DataType> = Promise<DataType> | ((signal: AbortSignal) => Promise<DataType>)
type AsyncState<DataType> =
    | {readonly status: "pending"}
    | {readonly status: "resolved", readonly value: DataType}
    | {readonly status: "rejected", readonly reason: unknown}
```

`AsyncRenderObjectOptions<DataType>` has `render`, `pending?`, `onFail?`, and `keepPrevious?`. See [Async data](/docs/velotype/async-data/).

## Lists

`class RenderObjectArray<DataType, UpdateRefsType = any>` and `class RenderTemplateArray<DataType, UpdateRefsType = any, RowElementType extends Element = HTMLElement>` have the same methods.

| Method | Description |
|---|---|
| `push(data)` / `pushAll(data[])` | Add to the end |
| `insertAt(index, data)` / `insertAllAt(index, data[])` | Insert before `index` |
| `deleteAt(startIndex, deleteCount?)` / `delete(data)` | Remove |
| `getAt(index)` / `setAt(index, data)` | Read and replace |
| `swap(indexA, indexB)` / `move(from, to)` | Reposition |
| `sort(compareFn)` / `reorder(indexes)` | Reorder |
| `filter(predicate?)` | Show only matching data points |
| `clear()` | Remove everything |
| `get length(): number` | The number of data points |

```ts
type RenderObjectArrayOptions<DataType, UpdateRefsType = any> = {
    wrapperElementTag?: string
    wrapperAttrs?: any
    renderFunction: RenderObjectRenderFunctionType<DataType, UpdateRefsType>
    handleUpdate?: RenderObjectHandleUpdateType<DataType, UpdateRefsType>
}

type RenderTemplateArrayOptions<DataType, UpdateRefsType = any, RowElementType extends Element = HTMLElement> = {
    wrapperElementTag?: string
    wrapperAttrs?: any
    template: RowElementType
    renderFunction: (row: RowElementType, data: DataType) => UpdateRefsType
    handleUpdate?: (row: RowElementType, updateRefs: UpdateRefsType, oldData: DataType, newData: DataType) => void
    on?: {[EventName in BubblingEventName]?: (event: HTMLElementEventMap[EventName], row: RowElementType, data: DataType, index: number) => void}
}
```

See [Lists](/docs/velotype/lists/).

## Events

| Export | Signature |
|---|---|
| `registerEventListener` | `(hasVtKey: HasVtKey, listeningKey: string, listener: VelotypeEventListener) => void` |
| `emitEvent` | `(listeningKey: string, event: VelotypeEvent, hasVtKey?: HasVtKey) => void` |
| `removeEventListeners` | `(hasVtKey: HasVtKey, listeningKey: string, listener?: VelotypeEventListener) => void` |
| `VelotypeEvent` | `class` with `constructor(emittingObject, event: string, data?: any)`, `emittingObject`, `event`, and `data` |

See [Events and errors](/docs/velotype/events-and-errors/).

## Styles and raw markup

| Export | Description |
|---|---|
| `setStylesheet(sheetText, sheetKey, resetSheet = false)` | Adds a stylesheet once per key |
| `HTML` | A Component that sets `innerHTML` on an HTML element. Attrs: `innerHTML`, `tag?`, `elementAttrs?` |
| `SVG` | A Component that sets `innerHTML` on an `<svg>` element. Attrs: `innerHTML`, `elementAttrs?` |
| `MATH` | A Component that sets `innerHTML` on a `<math>` element. Attrs: `innerHTML`, `elementAttrs?` |

See [Styling and raw HTML](/docs/velotype/styling-and-raw-html/).

## Types

| Type | Description |
|---|---|
| `FunctionComponent<AttrsType>` | `(attrs, children) => RenderableElements` |
| `EmptyAttrs` | The attrs type of a Component with no attrs |
| `IdAttr`, `StylePassthroughAttrs`, `ChildrenAttr` | Attrs mixins for `id`, `class` and `style`, and `children` |
| `RenderableElements` | Anything that can be a child: an element, text, a number, an Array of them, `null`, `undefined`, or a RenderObject |
| `AnchorElement` | `HTMLElement \| SVGSVGElement \| MathMLElement` |
| `BasicTypes` | `string \| bigint \| number \| boolean` |
| `RenderObjectRenderFunctionType`, `RenderObjectHandleUpdateType` | The function types of a RenderObject's render function and `handleUpdate` |
| `HasVtKey` | Something with a `vtKey`: a Component or RenderObject |
| `VelotypeEventListener` | `(event: VelotypeEvent) => void` |
| `StyleSection` | A stylesheet that `setStylesheet()` added |
| `HTMLAttrsType`, `SVGAttrsType`, `MATHAttrsType` | The attrs of `HTML`, `SVG`, and `MATH` |

The package also exports the DOM and JSX types (`HTMLAttributes`, event handler types, ARIA types, and CSS value types) that type-check TSX.

## Entry points

| Import | For |
|---|---|
| `@velotype/velotype` | The runtime, and the `jsx-runtime` |
| `@velotype/velotype/jsx-runtime` | The production JSX runtime |
| `@velotype/velotype/jsx-dev-runtime` | The development JSX runtime, with [hot reloading](/docs/velotype/development-tools/#hot-reloading) |
| `@velotype/velotype/devtools` | `__vtAppMetadata` (with `setEventTracer()` from 0.3.2) and `getDevtoolsHook()` |

Source: https://velotype.github.io/docs/velotype/devtools/

# Getting started

Velotype DevTools is a Chrome extension for debugging [Velotype](/docs/velotype/) apps. It adds three panels to Chrome DevTools, and a toolbar popup that shows whether Velotype is on the page.

| Panel | Shows |
|---|---|
| [Velotype](/docs/velotype/devtools/panels/#velotype) | The page's live component tree, and the fields of each component |
| [Velotype Events](/docs/velotype/devtools/panels/#velotype-events) | What is registered on the event bus |
| [VeloJSON](/docs/velotype/devtools/panels/#velojson) | VSON and VBIN payloads, decoded |

## Install

The extension is built from source, and loaded into Chrome as an unpacked extension. It needs [Deno](https://deno.com), and no npm or `node_modules`.

```sh
git clone https://github.com/Velotype/velodevtools
cd velodevtools
deno task build
```

`deno task build` copies the static files (including the icons) and bundles the extension into `dist/`. Then, in Chrome:

1. Open `chrome://extensions`
2. Turn on **Developer mode**
3. Choose **Load unpacked**, and select the `dist/` folder

Open DevTools on a page that uses Velotype, and the panels are in the tabs.

While developing the extension, `deno task watch` rebuilds on change. After it rebuilds, reload the extension from `chrome://extensions`, and refresh the inspected page, since content scripts are only injected on navigation. `deno task typecheck` checks the source.

## It needs the devtools hook

Velotype keeps the map from DOM elements to its live Component and RenderObject instances to itself. The extension reads it through a hook, `window.__VELOTYPE_DEVTOOLS_HOOK__`, which every current Velotype entry point installs. If a site uses Velotype and the tree is empty, its Velotype bundle predates the hook: update Velotype.

Several Velotype instances can be on one page (micro-frontends, or different versions in different bundles). Each registers separately with its own version, and their components do not collide.

## An app to try it on

This is a small Velotype app with fields worth looking at: a Component with attrs, a `RenderBasic`, a `RenderObject` that holds an object, a `Map`, and an event bus listener.

```tsx
import { Component, type EmptyAttrs, emitEvent, registerEventListener, RenderBasic, RenderObject, replaceElementWithRoot, VelotypeEvent } from "@velotype/velotype"

type Settings = {theme: string, notifications: {email: boolean, sms: boolean}, tags: Set<string>}

// A Component with fields to look at in the Velotype panel: attrs, a RenderBasic, a RenderObject
// holding an object (which expands to its live values), and a Map
class Profile extends Component<{name: string}> {
    visits = new RenderBasic<number>(0)
    settings = new RenderObject<Settings>(
        {theme: "dark", notifications: {email: true, sms: false}, tags: new Set(["admin", "beta"])},
        (settings: Settings) => <div>Theme: {settings.theme}</div>,
    )
    history: Map<string, number> = new Map([["login", 1], ["logout", 0]])

    // A listener, which the Velotype Events panel lists under the key "profile-updated"
    override mount() {
        registerEventListener(this, "profile-updated", () => { this.visits.value += 1 })
    }

    override render(attrs: Readonly<{name: string}>) {
        return <section>
            <h2>{attrs.name}</h2>
            <p>Visits: {this.visits}</p>
            {this.settings}
            <button type="button" onClick={() => emitEvent("profile-updated", new VelotypeEvent(this, "updated"))}>Update</button>
        </section>
    }
}

class App extends Component<EmptyAttrs> {
    override render() {
        return <main>
            <Profile name="Ada"/>
            <Profile name="Grace"/>
        </main>
    }
}

replaceElementWithRoot(<App/>, document.getElementById("app"))
```
Open it in a page, open DevTools, and look in the **Velotype** panel for `Profile`, and in **Velotype Events** for the `profile-updated` key.

---

Source: https://velotype.github.io/docs/velotype/devtools/panels/

# Panels

## Velotype

The live component tree for the page, like React DevTools. Each node shows its class name and its DOM anchor, the element it is attached to. For a class Component it also shows its `attrs` and its own instance fields, including the live values of `RenderObject` and `RenderBasic` fields.

* Click a node to inspect it, and the element is highlighted on the page
* Fields are an expand and collapse tree. An object, Array, Map, or Set field expands to its live values at any depth, fetched fresh from the page each time you expand it, and kept live for branches that are already expanded

A page with iframes shows each frame that has Velotype as its own root, labelled with its address.

Try it on the [demo app](/docs/velotype/devtools/#an-app-to-try-it-on): `Profile` has a `settings` RenderObject whose value is an object holding a nested object and a `Set`, and a `history` `Map`.

## Velotype Events

A snapshot of the event bus's current registrations: every listening key, how many listeners are on it, and, resolved against Velotype's registry, which live Components and RenderObjects they belong to.

It is useful for finding leaked listeners, and for checking that something is listening on a key at all. In the demo app, `profile-updated` has one listener for each `Profile`.

**Trace.** Press Start trace to list events as they are emitted, newest first: the listening key, the event's name, what emitted it, a summary of its data, and who was listening. Hover a component to highlight it on the page. The trace starts when you press Start and keeps the last 1,000 events, and Stop ends it. It needs Velotype 0.3.2 or later, which calls the extension's tracer just before the first listener of each event runs.

## VeloJSON

Decodes [velojson](/docs/velojson/) payloads.

**Network.** While the panel is open it inspects the bodies of network requests and responses, and lists those that are VSON or VBIN, decoded as JSON. A body is decoded when its `Content-Type` is `application/vson` or `application/vbin`. A `; charset=utf-8` suffix does not matter. A body with another content type is never attempted, and a body with one of these content types is always decoded, so a failure shows the real error.

Request bodies are read as the exact bytes your page sent. While the panel is open, the extension watches the page's `fetch`, `XMLHttpRequest`, and `navigator.sendBeacon` calls and keeps the bytes of VSON and VBIN bodies, so binary bodies decode correctly. A request that did not come from your page's JavaScript has no captured bytes and is not decoded.

The velojson docs' [browser](/docs/velojson/browser/) and the veloserver example below produce such responses:

```tsx
import { Router, Server } from "@velotype/veloserver"
import { VSON } from "@velotype/velojson"

// A server for trying the VeloJSON panel. The panel decodes a request or response body only when its
// Content-Type is application/vson or application/vbin (a "; charset=utf-8" suffix is fine).
const router = new Router<never>({})

router.get("/api/orders", () => {
    const orders = Array.from({length: 5}, (_, index) => ({id: index + 1, customer: "Ada", total: 9.99 * (index + 1)}))
    return new Response(VSON.encode(orders), {headers: {"content-type": "application/vson"}})
})

router.post("/api/orders", async (request) => {
    const order = VSON.decode(new Uint8Array(await request.arrayBuffer()))
    return new Response(VSON.encode({received: order}), {headers: {"content-type": "application/vson; charset=utf-8"}})
})

new Server(router).serve("127.0.0.1", 3000)
```
**Manual.** A decode tool turns bytes into JSON, and an encode tool turns JSON into bytes. Use it for a payload that has no content type, since it has no HTTP request to read one from.

**VBIN.** A VBIN payload can only be decoded in the debug format, where an object's keys are its numeric KeyIDs, such as `{"1": "hello"}`. The real field names come from a schema's `VBINObjectMapper`, which the extension cannot know for an arbitrary site. The panel labels VBIN output as such.

## The popup

The toolbar popup shows whether Velotype is present on the current page, without opening DevTools.

---

Source: https://velotype.github.io/docs/velotype/devtools/limitations/

# Known limitations

* **Request bodies are decoded only when your page sent them.** The extension keeps the bytes of a VSON or VBIN body sent with `fetch`, `XMLHttpRequest`, or `navigator.sendBeacon` while the VeloJSON panel is open, so a request made before the panel opened, or by a worker or the browser itself, is listed but not decoded. Chrome's network API gives a request body only as UTF-8 text, which would show corrupted bytes for a binary body, so the panel does not use it. A form post cannot send VSON or VBIN as binary anyway. Use the manual decode tool for those bytes. Response bodies are always decoded, because Chrome says whether they are base64
* **The event trace starts when you press Start,** and keeps the last 1,000 events. It needs Velotype 0.3.2 or later, and the registration table works with earlier versions
* **VSON and VBIN detection on the network tab uses the Content-Type.** velojson has a content type for each format, so the extension trusts it: a body with another content type is never guessed at from its bytes, and a body with one of these content types always shows its real decoding error. Use the manual decode tool for a body with no content type, such as `application/octet-stream`
* **VBIN is decoded in the debug format,** with KeyIDs as keys. The real field names come from a schema's mapper, which the extension cannot know for an arbitrary site. See [VeloJSON](/docs/velotype/devtools/panels/#velojson)
